products.name: Data Detox Kit

educational.note: Tactical Tech presents Data Detox Kit as everyday steps for digital privacy, security and wellbeing.

openness.note: The kit is freely available online and includes downloadable essential guides for privacy, security, wellbeing and misinformation.

depth.note: The resource covers multiple digital-life areas with practical guides, but it is designed for everyday action rather than advanced technical depth.

accessibility.note: The kit emphasizes simple everyday steps, though the main interactive site requires JavaScript and modern browsers.

calm.note: Data Detox is framed around reflective, step-by-step habit change rather than a feed or competitive course platform.

economical.note: The core Data Detox Kit materials are free to access and download.

products.description: A gentle, practical kit for learning how data traces, digital security, wellbeing, and misinformation shape everyday life online.

products.name: Civic Online Reasoning

educational.note: DIG says the COR curriculum provides free lessons and assessments that teach students to evaluate online information.

openness.note: The curriculum is free and the COR site includes Creative Commons materials and public lesson collections.

depth.note: COR is based on research and classroom testing around questions of source, evidence and lateral reading.

accessibility.note: Lessons and assessments are classroom-ready and structured for teachers, though the framing is most natural in school contexts.

calm.note: The curriculum is lesson-based and deliberate, with no feed or attention-retention mechanics.

economical.note: COR materials are described as free.

products.description: A research-backed media-literacy curriculum for evaluating online claims, sources, evidence, and social-media information.

products.name: RumorGuard

educational.note: The News Literacy Project says RumorGuard provides timely news-literacy lessons based on trending examples of misinformation.

openness.note: RumorGuard is publicly reachable as a web resource, but it is a hosted NLP project rather than an open-license curriculum commons.

depth.note: Entries include a quick debunk, takeaway tips, five credibility factors and links to related fact-checking resources.

accessibility.note: The site organizes recent viral false claims chronologically and by tags, making classroom discussion examples easy to find.

calm.note: The format turns viral claims into structured learning examples, though it still starts from current online rumors.

economical.note: NLP presents RumorGuard as a public educator resource rather than a paid course.

products.description: A public misinformation-learning site that turns real viral claims into source-checking lessons and credibility-factor practice.

products.name: CTRL-F

educational.note: CTRL-F teaches online search, verification, AI literacy and media-examining skills through lessons, videos, games and live web examples.

openness.note: CTRL-F provides public classroom resources, while published research notes curriculum materials and assessments were shared as supplemental materials.

depth.note: The verification curriculum teaches lateral reading, source investigation, claim checking and tracing information to original contexts.

accessibility.note: CTRL-F lessons are designed for grades 4-8 or grades 7-12 depending on track, with games, videos, activities and live examples.

calm.note: Lessons are classroom-structured and evidence-focused rather than feed-driven, with practice on search and verification habits.

economical.note: CTRL-F resource access is public and oriented to educators, with no consumer subscription described on its resource overview.

products.description: An evidence-backed digital media literacy curriculum for lateral reading, search, AI-generated content and online source verification.

products.name: MediaSmarts

educational.note: MediaSmarts' framework classifies digital media literacy around access, use, understand and engage for school learning.

openness.note: The framework page links teacher resources, curriculum outcomes, printable materials and parent tip sheets, though it is not a generic open-license repository.

depth.note: The framework spans nine digital media literacy topics, from reading media and representation to networked media and responsible engagement.

accessibility.note: Resources are linked to K-12 curriculum outcomes and parent/school supports, especially for Canadian educators.

calm.note: The framework supports deliberate classroom planning and parent guidance rather than attention-feed learning.

economical.note: Core framework and linked educational pages are public web resources, though some programs and contexts may depend on school implementation.

products.description: A Canadian digital and media literacy resource hub with K-12 framework materials, teacher resources and parent/school supports.

products.name: Navigating Digital Information

educational.note: Digital Inquiry Group describes the Crash Course series as research-based practical advice for navigating digital content.

openness.note: The series is publicly available as online videos, but it is a video course rather than an open remixable curriculum package.

depth.note: Topics include lateral reading, Wikipedia research, evaluating photos/videos, misleading data/infographics and social-media information.

accessibility.note: Short hosted videos with John Green make verification habits approachable for beginners and classroom use.

calm.note: Video episodes are bounded and educational, but the YouTube delivery path is less calm than a text curriculum or offline guide.

economical.note: The series is linked as public online video learning, with no course fee described by Digital Inquiry Group.

products.description: A beginner-friendly video series on lateral reading, source checking, images, data, Wikipedia and social-media information traps.

products.name: Bellingcat Online Investigation Toolkit

educational.note: The toolkit teaches open-source researchers how to find tools for verification, social media, mapping, archiving and other investigation tasks.

openness.note: Bellingcat says most included tools can be used for free and the toolkit can be downloaded as CSV by category.

depth.note: Bellingcat says entries include in-depth descriptions, common use cases and requirements or limitations for tools.

accessibility.note: The toolkit helps users choose tools, but OSINT workflows are more advanced than ordinary school media-literacy lessons.

calm.note: A categorized toolkit supports deliberate investigation, though the underlying topics can involve fast-moving online evidence.

economical.note: Bellingcat reports that most tools included in the toolkit can be used for free.

products.description: A serious open-source investigation toolkit for verification, archiving, geolocation, social-platform research and evidence workflows.

products.name: Bad News Game

educational.note: Cambridge's Social Decision-Making Lab describes Bad News as a theory-driven intervention for building resistance to online misinformation.

openness.note: The game is freely available for non-commercial use, but it is not presented as an open-source courseware project.

depth.note: The research page lists open-access publications and explains the inoculation model behind the misinformation training.

accessibility.note: A short browser game is easier to try than a full course and can be used in classrooms or informal learning.

calm.note: The game is bounded and educational, but it intentionally simulates manipulation tactics and social-media dynamics.

economical.note: Cambridge says the game is freely available for non-commercial use.

products.description: A short research-backed game that teaches people to recognize common misinformation tactics through active inoculation practice.

products.name: MediaWise

educational.note: Poynter says MediaWise teaches digital media literacy and fact-checking skills to help people spot misinformation and disinformation.

openness.note: MediaWise publishes free public media-literacy resources, but its materials are not a fully open courseware commons.

depth.note: MediaWise offers courses and curricula, including a self-directed Digital Media Literacy 101 resource, but much of the work is short-form training.

accessibility.note: The program is designed for people of different ages and includes student-facing resources and bite-sized curricula.

calm.note: MediaWise is useful and public-interest oriented, but some outreach is social-first and video-based rather than a quiet reference library.

economical.note: The student resources page lists free self-directed media-literacy learning materials.

products.description: A Poynter media-literacy initiative that teaches practical fact-checking habits for online rumors, feeds, and misinformation.

products.name: Be Internet Awesome

educational.note: Google describes Be Internet Awesome as a program that helps kids learn safe, confident online habits.

openness.note: The educator curriculum is free and publicly available, but it is a Google-branded program rather than an independent open commons.

depth.note: The curriculum covers five digital-safety topics with lesson plans, activities and worksheets, but it is an introductory K-12 resource.

accessibility.note: The program is built for educators and kids, with classroom materials and a game-like Interland activity.

calm.note: It is curriculum-oriented, though the Google-branded game layer is more playful and less quiet than a reference guide.

economical.note: The curriculum and program materials are free to access.

products.description: A free Google digital-citizenship curriculum for children, useful for safety basics but less independent than nonprofit alternatives.

products.name: DigitalLearn

educational.note: PLA describes DigitalLearn.org as self-directed courses that build digital literacy skills and confidence with technology.

openness.note: DigitalLearn states that its work is licensed under a Creative Commons BY-NC-SA license, with trainer materials available for libraries.

depth.note: Courses cover basic computer use, websites, search, email, video conferencing, privacy, scams, job skills, cloud storage and mobile devices.

accessibility.note: PLA says courses are self-directed, available in English and Spanish, and freely available to everyone.

calm.note: Short, self-paced modules and library workshop materials make it a calm basic-skills path rather than a feed or credential funnel.

economical.note: PLA says access to DigitalLearn.org is completely free to all users.

products.description: A public-library digital-literacy course hub for basic computer, internet, email, privacy, scam, job-search and mobile-device skills.

products.name: Applied Digital Skills

educational.note: Google describes Applied Digital Skills as a project-based online digital-skills curriculum for practical life, school and work tasks.

openness.note: The curriculum is free to use, but it is Google-hosted and platform-branded rather than a community-governed open courseware commons.

depth.note: Lessons use videos to guide learners through building projects from scratch, such as resumes, planning sheets and interactive stories.

accessibility.note: Google says the materials are appropriate for a wide range of learners, from middle school to college and beyond.

calm.note: The resource is structured as project lessons, though it sits inside a vendor learning platform rather than an independent public library model.

economical.note: Google states that Applied Digital Skills is free of charge.

products.description: A free project-based curriculum for practicing everyday digital tasks, especially Google Workspace-style school and work skills.

products.name: Microsoft Digital Literacy

educational.note: Microsoft frames the course around using devices, software and the internet to collaborate, discover, use and create information.

openness.note: Microsoft says the Digital Literacy material is licensed CC BY-NC-SA and provides downloadable course resources.

depth.note: The pathway covers computer use, online work and collaboration, information access, safe participation, digital content creation and digital content management.

accessibility.note: Microsoft says the course is for anyone with basic reading skills and is written at a newspaper-like reading level.

calm.note: A course pathway, downloadable resources and certificates support structured learning rather than social-feed engagement.

economical.note: Microsoft publishes the course and downloadable resources publicly for learners and educators.

products.description: A free basic digital-literacy pathway for people learning computers, online collaboration, internet use, safety and digital content basics.

products.name: Internet Matters

educational.note: Internet Matters provides online-safety advice, practical tools and resources to help children stay safe and thrive online.

openness.note: The site provides public guides, toolkits and printable resources, though it is not presented as open-licensed courseware.

depth.note: Topics include device safety settings, online issues, age-appropriate apps, conversation tips, screen time, parental controls, AI safety and family activities.

accessibility.note: The site offers tailored advice for families and free printable e-safety leaflets for home and classroom use.

calm.note: Guides, checklists and family toolkits support practical discussion, though some current-topic coverage updates like a live advice site.

economical.note: Its advice, leaflets and family safety resources are available publicly without a learner fee.

products.description: A family-focused online-safety hub with practical advice, device settings, checklists and tailored resources for children and caregivers.

products.name: NetSmartz

educational.note: NCMEC describes NetSmartz as its online safety education program with age-appropriate videos and activities for children.

openness.note: NetSmartz provides public teaching resources for students, families, educators and communities, though not as open-licensed curriculum.

depth.note: Resources include presentations, videos, activities and expert tips tailored for parents, communities, teens, tweens and younger children.

accessibility.note: NCMEC says the free collection supports families and students in grades K-12 and helps educators create internet-safety curricula.

calm.note: The resource is mission-driven and educational, but videos and kid-facing activities are more interactive than a quiet reference guide.

economical.note: The resources page describes NetSmartz teaching materials as a free collection for families and students.

products.description: A youth online-safety education program from NCMEC with free K-12 videos, presentations and activities for families and educators.

products.name: Better Internet for Kids

educational.note: The EU BIK+ strategy aims to ensure children are protected, empowered and respected online through age-appropriate digital services and resources.

openness.note: The platform provides public knowledge-hub material, resources, learning corners and links to national Safer Internet Centres.

depth.note: BIK combines policy, reports, good-practice guides, learning corners, youth participation, Safer Internet Centres and helpline/hotline data.

accessibility.note: Separate learning corners address children and youth, parents and caregivers, and teachers, but the broader platform is EU-policy heavy.

calm.note: The resource is organized as a public information and policy hub rather than an engagement-driven learning feed.

economical.note: The EU platform, learning corners and policy/resource pages are publicly available online.

products.description: An EU public hub for child online safety, digital citizenship, policy, Safer Internet Centres and educator/family learning resources.

products.name: Secure Our World

educational.note: CISA's Secure Our World program provides public cybersecurity-awareness resources and guidance.

openness.note: The resources are public government materials, though the program is a campaign rather than open courseware.

depth.note: Secure Our World is strongest for basic cyber hygiene and awareness; deeper organizational training sits in other CISA materials.

accessibility.note: CISA organizes the program around plain cybersecurity actions for individuals, families and partners.

calm.note: The materials are static public-service guidance, not a feed or gamified learning platform.

economical.note: CISA cybersecurity-awareness resources are publicly available without a learner fee.

products.description: A public cybersecurity-awareness resource for basic account, device, phishing, update, and password hygiene.

products.name: Internet Health

educational.note: Mozilla frames internet health around privacy, openness, inclusion and trustworthy AI as public-interest digital-literacy themes.

openness.note: Mozilla's internet-health materials are publicly accessible and aligned with open-web advocacy.

depth.note: The Internet Health framing connects several systemic issues, but it is more a public-interest explainer hub than a full structured course.

accessibility.note: The overview is readable and public, though some related research and policy material is better suited to adult learners.

calm.note: Mozilla's internet-health material is an editorial/public-interest resource rather than a feed-driven learning platform.

economical.note: The Internet Health overview and related Mozilla Foundation materials are free to read.

products.description: A Mozilla Foundation explainer hub for thinking about privacy, openness, inclusion, trustworthy AI, and healthier internet systems.

products.name: FTC Online Security

educational.note: FTC Online Security collects plain-language advice on passwords, malware, account recovery, public Wi-Fi, home Wi-Fi and device privacy.

openness.note: The materials are public government consumer-advice pages with articles and alerts, though not open courseware.

depth.note: The hub covers many common consumer-security topics, but each article is practical guidance rather than a deep technical curriculum.

accessibility.note: FTC advice is organized for ordinary consumers and includes Spanish-language access on the topic pages.

calm.note: The site is static public-service guidance and consumer alerts, not a feed-driven or gamified learning platform.

economical.note: FTC consumer-advice materials are free to read.

products.description: A plain government advice hub for consumer-level online security, scams, account recovery, malware, Wi-Fi, and privacy basics.

products.name: IdentityTheft.gov

educational.note: The FTC describes IdentityTheft.gov as the federal government's one-stop resource for reporting and recovering from identity theft.

openness.note: The recovery guidance, checklists and sample letters are public government resources rather than a private paid service.

depth.note: The site provides step-by-step recovery advice and forms, but it is focused on identity-theft response rather than broad digital-security education.

accessibility.note: The FTC says the site provides step-by-step advice, easy-to-print checklists and sample letters.

calm.note: The workflow is a practical recovery aid, though people usually arrive during a stressful incident rather than casual learning.

economical.note: IdentityTheft.gov is a free public federal service.

products.description: A US federal identity-theft reporting and recovery path with checklists, letters, and step-by-step remediation guidance.

products.name: Stay Safe Online

educational.note: NCA describes Stay Safe Online as a large collection of online safety resources, including articles, videos, infographics and toolkits.

openness.note: The resources are public and free to read, but the site is a nonprofit awareness hub rather than open-licensed courseware.

depth.note: The hub lists more than 100 articles plus videos and toolkits, with strongest depth for mainstream cyber hygiene and scams.

accessibility.note: NCA frames the resources for home, work, school and community awareness rather than specialist security teams only.

calm.note: The resource library is practical and topical, though newsletter, campaign and article feeds make it less quiet than a textbook-like reference.

economical.note: The public resources are free to access.

products.description: A broad nonprofit cyber-safety library with articles, videos, infographics, and toolkits for ordinary households and communities.

products.name: Privacy Rights Clearinghouse

educational.note: Privacy Rights Clearinghouse publishes privacy topics, reports, law overviews, a breach chronology, Q&A and data-broker resources.

openness.note: The nonprofit makes its consumer privacy resources public, including law overviews and rights-focused explainers.

depth.note: The site combines issue guides, state-law overviews, reports and a data-breach chronology, giving it stronger depth than basic privacy tips.

accessibility.note: The materials are readable for consumers but often law- and policy-oriented, making them denser than quick safety guides.

calm.note: The site is a nonprofit reference and advocacy hub, not an ad-driven feed or course marketplace.

economical.note: Privacy Rights Clearinghouse resources are free to read online.

products.description: A nonprofit privacy-rights reference for US privacy law, data brokers, breaches, and consumer rights.

products.name: EPIC

educational.note: EPIC works on consumer privacy, surveillance oversight, AI and human rights, platform accountability, open government and privacy law.

openness.note: EPIC is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit research and advocacy center with public analysis, updates and publications.

depth.note: EPIC's work includes litigation, FOIA/open-government records, expert advice to policymakers and detailed issue-area analysis.

accessibility.note: The material is valuable for adult civic learners, but legal and policy framing can be less beginner-friendly than consumer tip sheets.

calm.note: EPIC is a public-interest research and advocacy site rather than a social feed or commercial learning platform.

economical.note: EPIC's public analysis and issue pages are free to read online.

products.description: A deep public-interest privacy research and advocacy hub for understanding surveillance, AI, platforms, consumer privacy, and data law.

products.name: Ranking Digital Rights

educational.note: RDR evaluates powerful digital platforms and telecom companies on how well they uphold privacy, expression and other human rights.

openness.note: RDR publishes public indexes, company rankings, news and methodology-oriented research on corporate digital rights.

depth.note: The site includes 2026 telecom and 2025 big-tech index work, past assessments and investor guidance, making it a deeper accountability resource.

accessibility.note: The ranking format is easier to scan than legal filings, but the human-rights methodology and company research remain adult-level.

calm.note: RDR is an index and research site, not an algorithmic learning feed or gamified course.

economical.note: RDR rankings and research are public to read online.

products.description: A corporate-accountability index for seeing how major platforms and telecoms handle privacy, expression, governance, and digital rights.

products.name: ConnectSafely

educational.note: ConnectSafely says it educates people of all ages about online safety, privacy, security and digital wellness.

openness.note: It publishes public guides, quick-guides, parent resources, educator guides, Spanish quick guides and topic hubs.

depth.note: ConnectSafely offers in-depth guides and quick guides across social media, gaming, family tech, misinformation, privacy and cyberbullying.

accessibility.note: The materials are written for parents, educators, youth, policymakers, seniors and other adults.

calm.note: ConnectSafely explicitly emphasizes research-informed policies rather than moral panic, though it also runs news, podcasts and events.

economical.note: ConnectSafely guides and safety resources are public online.

products.description: A practical nonprofit resource for families, educators, youth, and adults navigating online safety, privacy, security, media literacy, and digital wellness.

products.name: Cyberbullying Research Center

educational.note: The Center publishes free resources for educators, parents, students, health care providers and adult victims around cyberbullying and online safety.

openness.note: Its resource page offers free downloadable, research-informed materials and fact sheets.

depth.note: The site combines resources, laws, research summaries, statistics, journal articles and presentations, giving it more depth than a one-page safety tip sheet.

accessibility.note: Resources include practical guides, glossaries, scripts and parent/educator tools, including some Spanish translations.

calm.note: The tone is research-informed and practical; the subject matter can be emotionally serious, but the site is not feed- or outrage-driven.

economical.note: The listed resource materials are free to access and download.

products.description: A research-informed cyberbullying and online-safety library for parents, educators, students, and youth-serving adults.

products.name: Security in a Box

educational.note: Security in a Box covers digital-security tools and tactics across identity, communications, devices, internet connections and files.

openness.note: The online toolkit is freely accessible and available in multiple languages.

depth.note: The toolkit goes beyond basics into threat assessment, device security, censorship circumvention, anonymizing connections and sensitive-file handling.

accessibility.note: The structure is task-based, but parts are designed for activists and higher-risk users, so beginners may need to move slowly.

calm.note: The site is a quiet reference toolkit rather than a feed or gamified course.

economical.note: Security in a Box is free to access online.

products.description: A deep digital-security toolkit for activists and higher-risk users, with practical sections on accounts, devices, communications, censorship, and files.

products.name: *Privacy Not Included

educational.note: Mozilla's guide helps consumers shop for connected products and apps with privacy and security in mind.

openness.note: The reviews, methodology and privacy tips are public from Mozilla Foundation, a nonprofit public-interest organization.

depth.note: Mozilla's methodology reviews privacy policies, company websites, news reports, research, app-store listings and other public information.

accessibility.note: The guide is built around product search, expert reviews, warning labels and practical tips for consumers.

calm.note: The buyer-guide framing is practical and skimmable, though creepiness sorting and warning labels make it more alert-driven than a quiet curriculum.

economical.note: The buyer's guide and methodology are free to access.

products.description: A Mozilla Foundation buyer's guide that teaches people how to read connected products, apps, data practices, security claims, and AI risks.

products.name: GCA Cybersecurity Toolkit

educational.note: GCA Cybersecurity Toolkits provide free tools for individuals and organizations to reduce cyber risk and implement basic security hygiene.

openness.note: The toolkit is publicly available and includes specialized toolkits for individuals, small businesses, journalists, mission-based organizations and elections.

depth.note: The toolkit maps practical tools and guidance to common security needs, but it is implementation-oriented rather than a full cyber curriculum.

accessibility.note: GCA says its free tools do not require advanced IT knowledge and classify tool levels by technical difficulty.

calm.note: The toolkits are organized as practical checklists and tools, though the site requires JavaScript for full use.

economical.note: GCA describes the cybersecurity toolkits and listed tools as free to use.

products.description: A practical cybersecurity toolkit hub for individuals, small businesses, journalists, mission-based organizations, and elections teams.

products.name: ReportFraud.gov

educational.note: The FTC describes ReportFraud.gov as the federal government's website for reporting fraud, scams and bad business practices.

openness.note: The reporting path and related consumer advice are public government resources rather than a private complaint service.

depth.note: ReportFraud.gov is strongest as a reporting and triage path, not a deep course on scams or digital security.

accessibility.note: The FTC says the platform was created to let consumers report fraud and receive streamlined advice.

calm.note: It is a practical reporting workflow, though people usually use it after a stressful scam or bad-business incident.

economical.note: ReportFraud.gov is a free FTC reporting service.

products.description: A US federal path for reporting scams, fraud, and bad business practices, with follow-up advice from the FTC.

products.name: Internet Crime Complaint Center

educational.note: IC3 describes itself as the central hub for reporting cyber-enabled crime, including cyber-enabled fraud, scams and cybercrime.

openness.note: IC3 publishes public service announcements, brochures, annual reports, resources and crime-specific information.

depth.note: The site combines reporting with alerts and annual reports, but it is law-enforcement intake and awareness rather than a full curriculum.

accessibility.note: IC3 tells victims to file even if unsure whether a complaint qualifies, while noting immediate danger belongs with emergency services.

calm.note: The reporting process is sober and official, but naturally incident-focused and less calm than preventive education.

economical.note: IC3 complaint submission and public resources are free.

products.description: The FBI's cybercrime reporting hub, useful for internet crime, scam awareness, annual reports, and official alerts.

products.name: Take It Down

educational.note: NCMEC says Take It Down helps remove or stop sharing of explicit images or videos taken before a person was 18.

openness.note: The service is public, free and available in many languages, but it depends on participating platforms.

depth.note: Take It Down explains who it is for, how hashing works, platform limits and additional NCMEC support routes.

accessibility.note: The site says people can remain anonymous and do not have to send images or videos to anyone; only hashes are provided.

calm.note: The resource uses a supportive crisis-aware tone, though it addresses a distressing situation.

economical.note: NCMEC describes Take It Down as a free service.

products.description: A free NCMEC service that uses privacy-preserving hashes to help stop online sharing of explicit images taken before someone was 18.

products.name: StopNCII.org

educational.note: SWGfL describes StopNCII.org as a free global tool to help adults protect intimate images from being shared online.

openness.note: The tool is public and free, but matching depends on participating platforms.

depth.note: StopNCII explains hashing, case tracking and partner-platform moderation, but it is a focused intervention rather than broad digital-safety training.

accessibility.note: SWGfL says images never leave the user's device; hashes are submitted instead.

calm.note: The tool is survivor-oriented and privacy-protective, though the use case is urgent and emotionally difficult.

economical.note: SWGfL describes StopNCII.org as free.

products.description: A free global hash-based tool for adults trying to prevent or reduce nonconsensual sharing of intimate images on participating platforms.

products.name: CCRI Safety Center

educational.note: CCRI Safety Center offers step-by-step resources for victims and survivors of image-based sexual abuse.

openness.note: The safety center is public and includes resource highlights, definitions, state laws, documentation guidance and support routes.

depth.note: The guide covers safety, terminology, rights, evidence preservation, removal requests, legal paths and support resources.

accessibility.note: The site is detailed and supportive, but the legal and evidence-preservation guidance is adult-level and can be dense.

calm.note: CCRI uses a survivor-centered tone and quick-exit design, though the subject matter is inherently serious.

economical.note: CCRI states its Image Abuse Helpline is available free of charge, and the safety-center resources are public.

products.description: A detailed safety and rights guide for adults dealing with image-based abuse, including documentation, removal, legal, and support paths.

products.name: StopBullying.gov
products.brand: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

educational.note: StopBullying.gov provides government information on bullying, cyberbullying, prevention, response, laws and youth resources.

openness.note: The public .gov site collects information from multiple government agencies and is managed by HHS.

depth.note: Cyberbullying sections cover tactics, prevention, social media, gaming, AI, parent awareness, teacher tips and reporting.

accessibility.note: The site includes sections for kids, parents, schools and communities, with plain-language help and videos.

calm.note: The tone is public-health oriented and prevention-focused, not a fear-driven feed.

economical.note: StopBullying.gov resources are free public government materials.

products.description: A government cyberbullying and bullying-prevention hub for youth, parents, educators, schools, and communities.

products.name: Small Business Cybersecurity Corner

educational.note: NIST's Small Business Cybersecurity Corner organizes cybersecurity basics, framework guidance, quick-start guides, sector guidance and topic guidance.

openness.note: NIST says included resources must be publicly available, accurate, comprehensive for a cybersecurity risk area and freely available to use.

depth.note: Topic guidance spans MFA, phishing, privacy, ransomware, incident response, scams, cloud security, data/device security and network connections.

accessibility.note: The hub is tailored to small-business needs, though some NIST and framework materials remain denser than consumer tip sheets.

calm.note: The site is an official reference hub without feeds or gamified pressure.

economical.note: NIST says resources listed for inclusion must be freely available for others to use.

products.description: An official NIST cybersecurity resource hub for small organizations that need practical guides without enterprise-security overhead.

products.name: Digital Defense Fund Guides

educational.note: DDF publishes digital-security guides for abortion privacy, organizational security, border security, social media, VPNs, data breaches and related risks.

openness.note: DDF's guide library and learn resources are publicly accessible, with some Spanish-language resources.

depth.note: The guide list covers both individual privacy risks and organizational security needs, including checklists, admin guides and breach response.

accessibility.note: The resources are practical and movement-oriented, though some topics assume high-risk context and careful safety planning.

calm.note: DDF frames digital security as practical support, not an engagement platform, while centering sensitive and higher-risk situations.

economical.note: DDF says its trainings are free and open to people working in allied movements, and its guide resources are public.

products.description: A practical guide library for reproductive-justice digital security, privacy, organizational security, breach response, social media, and safer web infrastructure.

products.name: Safety Net Project

educational.note: NNEDV's Safety Net Project develops technology safety and privacy resources for agencies and survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking and trafficking.

openness.note: Safety Net publishes public technology toolkits and survivor-facing resources.

depth.note: The project covers safety planning, intimate image abuse, AI, stalkerware, online data, tech policy and technology-facilitated advocacy.

accessibility.note: Survivor resources point to hotlines and practical toolkits, but safety changes can be context-sensitive and may need advocate support.

calm.note: The project is survivor-centered and safety-planning oriented rather than feed-driven.

economical.note: The technology safety resources and survivor toolkits are public online.

products.description: A survivor-centered technology safety resource hub for domestic violence, stalking, sexual assault, trafficking, and technology-facilitated abuse contexts.

products.name: Clinic to End Tech Abuse

educational.note: CETA helps survivors and service providers understand how technology is used to facilitate harm and how survivors can stay safer.

openness.note: CETA publishes free resources and guides, including account safety guides, platform settings and cyberharassment documentation.

depth.note: Resources cover social media settings, Google/Android, Apple/iCloud, smart-home trackers, spyware checks, separation checklists and training requests.

accessibility.note: The guides are free and practical, but direct clinic service is focused on survivors in New York City.

calm.note: The site has a quick-exit affordance and survivor-safety framing rather than engagement mechanics.

economical.note: CETA says its resources and how-to guides are free to download and use.

products.description: A Cornell Tech clinic and resource hub for technology-facilitated abuse, with practical safety guides and a NYC-focused survivor service.

products.name: Coalition Against Stalkerware

educational.note: The coalition explains stalkerware, survivor risks, technology-facilitated abuse and how support organizations and tech companies can respond.

openness.note: The site is public, multilingual and backed by a coalition of domestic-violence organizations and IT security companies.

depth.note: It covers the issue of stalkerware, survivor information, professional resources, tech-company guidance, news and partner expertise.

accessibility.note: The site includes an exit link, multiple languages and survivor-specific information, though device-safety action can require advocate support.

calm.note: The site is support-oriented and educational, but the subject involves active safety risks and should be approached carefully.

economical.note: Coalition information and resources are public online.

products.description: A multilingual public-interest resource explaining stalkerware and technology-facilitated abuse, with guidance for survivors, professionals, and tech companies.

products.name: Online Harassment Field Manual

educational.note: PEN America's field manual offers concrete strategies for defending yourself and others against online abuse.

openness.note: The public manual is available in multiple languages and is organized for targets, witnesses/allies and employers.

depth.note: The manual covers preparation, response, self-care, legal considerations, support, definitions and institutional best practices.

accessibility.note: The manual is practical and navigable, but the depth and legal/safety topics are best for older teens and adults.

calm.note: It frames online abuse as a safety and expression issue with structured response options rather than outrage engagement.

economical.note: The field manual is free to read online.

products.description: A deep online-harassment field manual for preparing, responding, documenting, finding support, and protecting free expression under abuse.

products.name: Elements of AI

educational.note: Elements of AI is a free online course series created by MinnaLearn and the University of Helsinki to introduce AI to non-experts.

openness.note: The course is free and openly accessible online, though it is a hosted course rather than a reusable open-source curriculum repository.

depth.note: University of Helsinki describes the course as broad, practical and expert-created, but introductory rather than a technical ML degree path.

accessibility.note: The course is designed for a broad audience without requiring complicated mathematics or programming.

calm.note: Self-paced course structure supports deliberate learning rather than feed-driven discovery or social competition.

economical.note: Elements of AI describes the courses as free online courses.

products.description: A calm, free introductory AI course for adults who want to understand what AI can and cannot do without jumping straight into coding.

products.name: AI Pedagogy Project

educational.note: AI Pedagogy Project offers educator resources and assignments for critical and creative engagement with AI in education.

openness.note: The project publishes public AI guides and curated assignments, though reuse terms vary by resource.

depth.note: metaLAB frames the project around critical questions of language, ownership, authorship, rights and agency, giving it stronger humanities depth than basic prompt tips.

accessibility.note: The materials are useful for educators, but the humanities and classroom-assignment framing is less immediately accessible for casual learners.

calm.note: The resource is assignment- and guide-based, without algorithmic feeds, urgency mechanics or marketplace pressure.

economical.note: The project resources are publicly accessible online without a learner fee.

products.description: A critical AI teaching resource for educators who want assignments that discuss capability, limitation, authorship, rights, and agency.

products.name: AI4K12

educational.note: AI4K12 is developing national guidelines, a resource directory and a practitioner community for K-12 AI education.

openness.note: AI4K12 publishes public guidelines and a curated resource directory, though it is a standards/resource hub rather than one complete open textbook.

depth.note: The guidelines organize AI learning around grade-band knowledge, skills and the 5 Big Ideas in AI.

accessibility.note: The resource directory and curriculum materials help educators find age-appropriate materials, but the site is more useful for teachers than self-directed learners.

calm.note: AI4K12 is a standards and curriculum hub, not an attention-feed learning platform.

economical.note: AI4K12 guidelines and curriculum-resource pages are publicly available online.

products.description: A K-12 AI education standards and resource hub for teachers trying to make AI concepts age-appropriate and less hype-driven.

products.name: AI Guidance for Schools Toolkit

educational.note: TeachAI's toolkit helps education leaders and teachers create guidance for using AI in primary and secondary education while mitigating risks.

openness.note: The toolkit is publicly available and includes editable guidance materials, but it is policy guidance rather than open courseware.

depth.note: The toolkit covers vision, principles, risk, policy examples and sample guidance for AI in schools.

accessibility.note: The material is designed for education authorities, school leaders and teachers, so it is practical but less student-facing.

calm.note: The toolkit is structured policy guidance, not a feed, marketplace or gamified learning app.

economical.note: TeachAI makes the toolkit resources available online without a learner fee.

products.description: A practical AI-in-schools policy toolkit for leaders and teachers trying to allow useful AI while naming risks clearly.

products.name: Day of AI

educational.note: Day of AI brings MIT RAISE-developed AI curriculum, tools, assessments and teacher professional-development materials to students and educators.

openness.note: Day of AI describes its tools and curriculum as free and open-source.

depth.note: MIT Open Learning describes Day of AI as hands-on lessons and activities organized by age group, strongest for introductory K-12 AI exposure.

accessibility.note: The curriculum was designed for educators with little or no technology background and for students across age groups.

calm.note: Day of AI is curriculum- and activity-based rather than feed-driven, though some hands-on classroom activities are more event-like than self-study.

economical.note: MIT Open Learning describes Day of AI resources as free.

products.description: A free MIT RAISE curriculum for introducing K-12 students to AI concepts, social effects, and hands-on classroom activities.

products.name: Machine Learning Crash Course

educational.note: Google describes the Machine Learning Crash Course as a practical introduction with animated videos, interactive visualizations and hands-on exercises.

openness.note: The course is free on Google Developers, but it is Google-hosted material rather than an independent open curriculum commons.

depth.note: Google's ML foundations page positions the crash course as a hands-on course for critical machine-learning basics.

accessibility.note: The course is beginner-oriented but still assumes comfort with technical concepts and practice exercises.

calm.note: The course is structured and self-paced, though badges, quizzes and developer-platform context make it less quiet than a public library-style resource.

economical.note: Google describes the Machine Learning Crash Course as free online training.

products.description: A free technical machine-learning course for learners ready to move from AI literacy into supervised learning, features, loss, and model evaluation.

products.name: Hugging Face Course

educational.note: The course teaches NLP, LLMs and the Hugging Face ecosystem through structured chapters and practical examples.

openness.note: Hugging Face publishes the course repository publicly and describes the course as free and open source.

depth.note: The course covers transformers, datasets, tokenizers, acceleration tooling and the Hub rather than only surface-level prompting.

accessibility.note: The course is online and free, but learners need some comfort with code and ML vocabulary.

calm.note: Chapter-based self-study makes it calmer than a feed or cohort funnel, though the surrounding platform is a large model hub.

economical.note: The course is available online for free.

products.description: A free open course for moving from basic AI literacy into practical NLP, transformers, datasets, and model-hub workflows.

products.name: Practical Deep Learning for Coders

educational.note: fast.ai describes the course as a practical deep-learning and machine-learning course for people with some coding experience.

openness.note: The course and related book materials are freely available online, though it is a course site rather than a fully generic OER repository.

depth.note: The course includes roughly nine substantial lessons and a second foundations-to-diffusion path for more experienced learners.

accessibility.note: The course reduces math prerequisites but still expects coding comfort and model-building persistence.

calm.note: The self-paced course-and-notebook structure supports deliberate practice rather than social feed consumption.

economical.note: fast.ai describes Practical Deep Learning for Coders as a free course.

products.description: A strong free path for coders who want practical deep-learning competence rather than just AI vocabulary.

products.name: Full Stack Deep Learning

educational.note: Full Stack Deep Learning teaches the lifecycle of AI-powered products, from problem definition and model choice to deployment and UX.

openness.note: The online course materials and GitBook are publicly hosted, though the broader community and events are not a public-domain curriculum commons.

depth.note: The course targets learners who already know deep-learning basics and want production-system depth.

accessibility.note: Prerequisites include Python, prior deep learning, version control and Unix-style engineering experience.

calm.note: Course-style lectures and materials are structured, though the professional-builder audience makes it more intense than civic AI literacy resources.

economical.note: Core course materials are publicly accessible online; costs may vary for live events or community offerings.

products.description: A deep builder-oriented resource for understanding the full lifecycle of AI products beyond model training alone.

products.name: AI for Beginners

educational.note: The curriculum covers AI through 12 weeks and 24 lessons with practical lessons, quizzes and labs.

openness.note: Microsoft hosts the curriculum publicly on GitHub with lesson source files and translations.

depth.note: The course covers beginner AI concepts, tools such as TensorFlow and PyTorch, and AI ethics, but remains introductory.

accessibility.note: Microsoft describes the curriculum as beginner-friendly, with multi-language support expanding accessibility.

calm.note: A fixed curriculum with lessons and quizzes supports intentional study rather than recommendation-feed browsing.

economical.note: The GitHub curriculum is publicly available without a learner fee.

products.description: A structured open GitHub curriculum for learners who want a broad beginner path through AI concepts, labs, and ethics.

products.name: Generative AI for Beginners

educational.note: Microsoft describes the curriculum as a 21-lesson course on building generative-AI applications.

openness.note: The lesson materials are publicly hosted on GitHub for reading, reuse and contribution.

depth.note: The course moves beyond prompting into application architecture and implementation patterns for generative AI.

accessibility.note: The course is beginner-oriented, but it is still aimed at learners building applications rather than general consumers.

calm.note: A lesson-based GitHub curriculum is more deliberate than short-form AI-tips content or viral prompt feeds.

economical.note: The curriculum is available publicly on GitHub without a learner fee.

products.description: A practical open curriculum for beginners who want to understand and build generative-AI applications.

products.name: Machine Learning for Beginners

educational.note: Microsoft describes the curriculum as a 12-week, 26-lesson course focused on classic machine learning.

openness.note: The curriculum is openly hosted on GitHub Pages and in a public repository.

depth.note: The curriculum covers classic machine learning with scikit-learn and avoids jumping directly to deep learning.

accessibility.note: The beginner framing and classic-ML focus are accessible, but the course still assumes comfort with exercises and code.

calm.note: A fixed 12-week curriculum gives learners a quiet path through ML foundations without platform-feed pressure.

economical.note: The curriculum is publicly available online without a learner fee.

products.description: A free classic-machine-learning curriculum for learners who want model basics before the generative-AI layer.

products.name: Experience AI

educational.note: Experience AI offers lesson materials for introducing AI and machine learning to learners aged 11 to 14.

openness.note: The programme provides free classroom resources and course materials, though it is curated by the partner organizations.

depth.note: The programme focuses on foundational AI understanding, social effects and classroom activities rather than advanced ML implementation.

accessibility.note: The resources are designed for educators and young learners, with versions for multiple countries and classroom contexts.

calm.note: Lesson packs and educator courses support structured teaching rather than attention-feed exploration.

economical.note: Raspberry Pi Foundation describes Experience AI as a free programme and course.

products.description: A free AI education programme for teachers and younger learners, especially useful for grounded classroom introduction.

products.name: AI Literacy Lessons for Grades 6-12

educational.note: The lessons help students think critically about AI, impacts, benefits, risks and responsible use.

openness.note: The lesson collection is publicly linked and classroom-ready, though it is a curated lesson set rather than an open textbook.

depth.note: The lessons are quick introductions to AI and social impacts, strongest as discussion starters rather than a full technical course.

accessibility.note: The collection is designed as grab-and-go lessons for grades 6-12, with many lessons around 20 minutes or less.

calm.note: Short classroom lesson plans make the topic discussable without pushing students toward AI-product feeds.

economical.note: Media Literacy Now lists the Common Sense lesson collection as free.

products.description: Short classroom AI-literacy lessons that focus on critical thinking, responsible use, and student-facing digital citizenship.

products.name: Intro to AI

educational.note: aiEDU describes Intro to AI as a 10-week project-based course for grades 9-12.

openness.note: aiEDU publishes access to AI literacy curriculum and resources, but the materials are an organized nonprofit programme rather than a fully open repository.

depth.note: The course includes 35 45-minute lessons, giving it more classroom depth than a single awareness lesson.

accessibility.note: The resource is teacher-led and designed for grades 9-12, so it is accessible in classrooms but less self-service for casual adults.

calm.note: Project-based lessons and educator support make it a structured curriculum rather than a high-pressure platform.

economical.note: aiEDU frames its curriculum work around broad access to AI literacy and lists the Intro to AI course for access online.

products.description: A nonprofit classroom AI-literacy curriculum for high-school students, built around project-based lessons rather than vendor tutorials.

products.name: Teachable Machine

educational.note: Teachable Machine lets learners train simple models using images, sounds and poses, making machine-learning behavior visible.

openness.note: The web tool is public and export-oriented, but it is Google-hosted rather than an independent open curriculum.

depth.note: The tool is intentionally simple and no-code, excellent for intuition but shallow for ML theory.

accessibility.note: Google describes it as a fast, easy way to create ML models with no expertise or coding required.

calm.note: It is a bounded project tool rather than an endless content feed, though use may involve webcam or microphone examples.

economical.note: The tool is available on the public web without a learner fee.

products.description: A no-code way to see how ML models learn from examples, useful for demystifying AI before diving into theory.

products.name: People + AI Guidebook

educational.note: The guidebook provides practical guidance and best practices for designing human-centered AI products.

openness.note: The guidebook is publicly available online, though it is Google-authored guidance rather than community-governed OER.

depth.note: The guidebook covers product-lifecycle considerations for useful and responsible AI rather than only AI terminology.

accessibility.note: The material is clearest for designers, product teams and builders, so it is less immediate for general consumers.

calm.note: Guidebook-style chapters support reflective design practice instead of feed-driven AI tips.

economical.note: The guidebook is publicly readable online.

products.description: A product-minded responsible-AI guide for people designing tools that should respect human needs and uncertainty.

products.name: AI Safety Courses

educational.note: BlueDot runs courses and projects for people who want to work on AI safety and frontier AI governance.

openness.note: Courses are free to start, but cohort access is selective and not all learning happens as fully open courseware.

depth.note: The AI governance course is a roughly 30-hour cohort course for people ready to engage seriously with frontier AI and AGI policy.

accessibility.note: Some courses require prerequisite knowledge, applications and cohort participation, so they are not beginner drop-in resources.

calm.note: Reading-and-discussion cohorts can support careful study, though application cycles and career framing add pressure.

economical.note: BlueDot invites learners to start for free and lists upcoming free courses and projects.

products.description: A deeper AI-safety and governance learning path for people ready to study frontier-risk questions seriously.

products.name: Datawrapper Academy

educational.note: Datawrapper Academy teaches chart, map and table creation through practical help articles and examples.

openness.note: The learning articles are public, but they are tied to Datawrapper's hosted visualization tool rather than neutral OER.

depth.note: The Academy includes over 100 feature and practice articles, strongest for applied chart literacy rather than statistics theory.

accessibility.note: Datawrapper emphasizes no-code visualization and getting started with charts, maps and tables.

calm.note: Help-article and tutorial navigation is intentional and task-based, not algorithmic content consumption.

economical.note: Datawrapper says its free plan supports unlimited creation, publishing, embedding and PNG export.

products.description: A practical data-visualization learning hub for building chart literacy through low-friction, no-code examples.

products.name: Data Science 4 Everyone

educational.note: DS4E advances K-12 data science education and provides learning progressions for data literacy, data science and foundational AI.

openness.note: The coalition publishes public reports, one-pagers and implementation resources for data-science education.

depth.note: The learning progressions outline national expectations and practices, but are more framework than complete learner course.

accessibility.note: The resources are most accessible to educators and policy leaders rather than individual self-paced learners.

calm.note: Reports and frameworks support deliberate curriculum planning without feed mechanics or credential pressure.

economical.note: Core reports, progressions and coalition resources are publicly accessible online.

products.description: A public data-literacy and data-science education coalition, useful for schools and curriculum planners more than casual learners.

products.name: The Data Journalism Handbook

educational.note: The handbook teaches how data is analyzed, created and used in journalism and public-interest media.

openness.note: The handbook is readable online and has open-access support through the Open Knowledge and Public Data Lab ecosystem.

depth.note: The second edition includes 54 chapters from 74 researchers and practitioners, giving it substantial field depth.

accessibility.note: The handbook is public and readable, but its critical data-practice framing is denser than beginner tutorials.

calm.note: A book-style resource supports slower reading and reflection about data claims, context and power.

economical.note: The handbook is available to read online without a fee.

products.description: An open handbook for understanding how data becomes public evidence, especially useful for news and civic literacy.

products.name: Apple Personal Safety User Guide

educational.note: Apple describes the guide as strategies for safeguarding accounts, devices and information, including small changes and severing unwanted digital ties.

openness.note: The guide is public and downloadable, but it is vendor documentation rather than open courseware.

depth.note: Coverage includes account, device, sharing and safety-check workflows, with special attention to technology-enabled abuse, stalking and harassment.

accessibility.note: Apple provides guided strategies, current-issue and plan-ahead paths, plus a PDF version for offline reference.

calm.note: The resource is a practical support guide without feeds, ads or gamified engagement mechanics.

economical.note: Apple Support makes the Personal Safety User Guide available free online.

products.description: A practical device-and-account safety guide, especially useful for people auditing sharing, location, account access, or technology-enabled abuse risks.

products.name: Google Safety Center

educational.note: Google Safety Center explains security, privacy controls, scam protection and family safety across Google products.

openness.note: The material is public and free to read, but it is company-controlled product guidance rather than open, independent curriculum.

depth.note: Coverage is broad and approachable, but mostly product-centered and lighter than independent security curricula.

accessibility.note: The center is built for mainstream users and links to practical controls such as account privacy settings.

calm.note: It is a static help-and-explainer site, though the framing is promotional and Google-product-centered.

economical.note: Google's safety and privacy explainers are available without a fee.

products.description: A mainstream, product-centered safety explainer for people who live in Google services and need the basic controls in plain language.

products.name: Internet Society Learning

educational.note: Internet Society Learning offers courses on how the Internet works, governance, network operations, security and community networks.

openness.note: Internet Society publicly invites people to take a free online course, though the learning platform is not the same as openly licensed courseware.

depth.note: Individual courses cover technical and governance topics such as Internet governance, critical Internet properties and network operations.

accessibility.note: Courses include both technical and non-technical topics, but some tracks assume networking or systems background.

calm.note: The course catalog is self-directed learning, not a feed or ad-driven attention product.

economical.note: Internet Society promotes free online courses as part of its learning program.

products.description: A strong route for people who want to understand the Internet as infrastructure, governance, networks, security, and community access.

products.name: ICANN Learn

educational.note: ICANN describes ICANN Learn as courses about how the Internet works, how it is governed, policy writing and public meeting participation.

openness.note: The learning route is public and free to register for, but course access typically runs through the ICANN Learn platform.

depth.note: ICANN Learn is useful for DNS, governance and policy participation, though narrower than a general internet-technology curriculum.

accessibility.note: ICANN frames the beginner materials as a way to get started with courses, infographics, videos and other resources.

calm.note: The platform is course and resource based rather than feed-based.

economical.note: ICANN's Universal Acceptance training page directs users to register for a free ICANN Learn course.

products.description: A focused path for learning DNS, internet governance, policy participation, and the institutional layer behind domain names.

products.name: LearnOSM

educational.note: LearnOSM provides step-by-step guides for contributing to and using OpenStreetMap.

openness.note: The resource teaches an open mapping ecosystem and is publicly available online.

depth.note: The guides cover beginner mapping and humanitarian coordination, but are more practical manual than deep geospatial course.

accessibility.note: LearnOSM is organized as easy-to-follow step-by-step learning materials for new mappers.

calm.note: The site is a manual-style learning resource without ads, feeds or gamified pressure.

economical.note: HOT's learning materials and LearnOSM-style training resources are free to access online.

products.description: A calm, practical route into open mapping and humanitarian geospatial literacy.

products.name: School of Data

educational.note: School of Data offers courses on data fundamentals, exploring data, mapping and using open data tools.

openness.note: The course catalog focuses on open data and public digital-literacy skills, with free courses visible in the catalog.

depth.note: Courses include structured multi-lesson modules, but the catalog is narrower than a full data-science platform.

accessibility.note: Introductory courses such as Data Fundamentals and a gentle mapping introduction make the path approachable.

calm.note: The resource is course-based and skills-oriented rather than feed-driven.

economical.note: The listed core courses are marked free in the public catalog.

products.description: A practical open-data learning hub for people building civic data, mapping and basic data-literacy skills.

products.name: The Glass Room

educational.note: Tactical Tech describes The Glass Room as an interactive exhibition for understanding how technologies and data are changing our lives.

openness.note: The Community Edition is designed for schools, libraries, festivals and community spaces, but full participation can depend on local hosts.

depth.note: It is strong for public engagement and discussion, but less deep than a long-form security or data-literacy curriculum.

accessibility.note: The Community Edition has been translated into more than 30 languages and designed as a lightweight pop-up exhibition.

calm.note: The project uses reflective exhibits and analog community discussion rather than an attention-optimized feed.

economical.note: Online project materials are free to browse, while in-person exhibits depend on host institutions and locations.

products.description: A public-facing privacy and data-literacy exhibition model for communities, libraries, schools and festivals.

products.name: Exposing the Invisible

educational.note: Exposing the Invisible brings together films, interviews, guides, tools and workshops for investigative techniques.

openness.note: The site publishes free learning resources, guides and investigative materials online.

depth.note: The Kit is a collaborative self-learning resource for investigative tools, evidence-building, verification, ethics and safety.

accessibility.note: The Kit aims to make experienced investigators' techniques accessible to motivated people and communities, though topics can be advanced.

calm.note: Materials are guide, film and workshop based rather than feed-based.

economical.note: Tactical Tech describes Exposing the Invisible as free, accessible and educational.

products.description: A deep open-investigation learning hub for verification, evidence-building, OSINT practice, ethics and safety.

products.name: Street-Level Surveillance

educational.note: EFF's Street-Level Surveillance project explains police surveillance technologies routinely deployed in communities.

openness.note: The field guide is public and free to read from EFF.

depth.note: Resources are designed for advocates, journalists, defense attorneys, policymakers and the public seeking straight explanations of surveillance equipment.

accessibility.note: The guide explains specific technologies in plain terms, though some legal and technical implications require care.

calm.note: The project is a reference guide rather than a feed, social platform or gamified course.

economical.note: EFF makes the field guide available freely online.

products.description: A practical field guide for understanding surveillance technologies such as license-plate readers, drones, face recognition and cell-site simulators.

products.name: Atlas of Surveillance

educational.note: EFF describes Atlas of Surveillance as a searchable database and map of surveillance technologies used by domestic law enforcement agencies in the United States.

openness.note: The Atlas is a public database built from crowdsourcing, data journalism and public/nonprofit datasets.

depth.note: The project documents technologies such as drones, body cameras, license-plate readers and facial recognition across agencies and jurisdictions.

accessibility.note: The map and database make local surveillance infrastructure explorable, though interpretation may require media-literacy context.

calm.note: The Atlas is a searchable civic-data resource rather than an engagement feed.

economical.note: The Atlas is publicly accessible without a fee.

products.description: A U.S.-specific civic-data map for seeing which surveillance technologies local law-enforcement agencies use.

products.name: Access Now Digital Security Helpline

educational.note: Access Now provides digital security guidance and recent guides for civil society, activists, journalists and human-rights defenders.

openness.note: The helpline is a free-of-charge resource and publishes guides, but personalized support is targeted to high-risk civil society users.

depth.note: Services include rapid incident response, personalized recommendations, censorship circumvention, shutdown support and safer communication guidance.

accessibility.note: The resource is strongest for activists, media organizations and human-rights defenders, so it is less general-purpose than mainstream safety guides.

calm.note: It is support-and-guide oriented, not a feed or ad-supported learning platform.

economical.note: Access Now says the helpline provides 24/7 free-of-charge technical support.

products.description: A high-risk-user digital security resource for civil society, activists, journalists and human-rights defenders.

products.name: The Influence Industry Project

educational.note: The project teaches how data-driven political campaigners, consultants, platforms and technology companies influence citizens.

openness.note: The site publishes research, learning materials and resources about digital political influence for public use.

depth.note: Tactical Tech frames the project as research, learning and exploration of the professional digital political influence industry.

accessibility.note: The materials are readable and public, but the topic is specialized and politically technical.

calm.note: The project is research-and-resource based rather than feed-driven.

economical.note: The public project site and resources are free to access.

products.description: A focused resource for understanding data-driven political influence, voter targeting, political technology and campaign-consulting ecosystems.

products.name: Mozilla AI Intersections Database

educational.note: Mozilla says the database maps intersections between social justice, human rights and documented AI impacts.

openness.note: The database is publicly browsable, but it is a curated research database rather than open courseware.

depth.note: The resource also catalogs civil-society organizations, social movement actors and researchers working at AI-impact intersections.

accessibility.note: It is useful for research and movement mapping, but less beginner-friendly than lesson-based AI-literacy courses.

calm.note: The database supports deliberate research rather than streaks, feeds or addictive engagement loops.

economical.note: Mozilla makes the database publicly accessible online.

products.description: A research map for connecting AI impacts to civil rights, data rights, labor, inclusion, movement work and human-rights questions.

products.name: Web Literacy for Student Fact-Checkers

educational.note: The book teaches concrete web fact-checking moves, including going upstream, reading laterally and tracing viral content.

openness.note: Pressbooks lists the book under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License.

depth.note: The table of contents covers previous work, source tracing, lateral reading, authority checks, scholarly signals and field techniques.

accessibility.note: The book is public and web-readable, though it is text-heavy and best for motivated learners or guided classes.

calm.note: The resource is a static open textbook, not a feed, dashboard or gamified platform.

economical.note: The full book is publicly readable on Pressbooks at no cost.

products.description: An open textbook teaching practical fact-checking habits for web claims, viral media, sources, scholars and online evidence.

products.name: UNESCO Media and Information Literacy e-Platform

educational.note: UNESCO says the platform provides a media and information literacy competency framework, modules and pedagogical suggestions.

openness.note: UNESCO says platform resources can be shared and used, with OER resources shareable, adaptable and re-uploadable by users.

depth.note: The platform covers MIL curriculum, audio MOOC, media-organization toolkit, policy and multi-language reference resources.

accessibility.note: The platform is international and multilingual, but it is denser than beginner classroom portals.

calm.note: UNESCO presents a reference and curriculum platform rather than an engagement feed.

economical.note: UNESCO describes the e-platform as providing access to MIL reference resources and tools.

products.description: A UNESCO media and information literacy hub for educators, learners, policymakers and researchers working on digital and information competency.

products.name: Web Security Academy

educational.note: PortSwigger describes Web Security Academy as free online web security training with learning materials and interactive labs.

openness.note: The training is free to access, but it is a proprietary platform connected to PortSwigger's product ecosystem.

depth.note: The academy covers many web vulnerability topics and includes hands-on labs for SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, APIs, Web LLM attacks and more.

accessibility.note: It is flexible and online, but technical learners benefit from setup knowledge and an account for progress tracking.

calm.note: The resource is skill-focused, though progress tracking, Hall of Fame and competitive lab solving add some gamified pressure.

economical.note: PortSwigger says the Academy is 100% free and can be used with Burp Suite Community Edition for free experimentation.

products.description: A deep, hands-on web application security training platform with labs for learners moving beyond basic digital safety into technical security.

products.name: OWASP WebGoat

educational.note: OWASP describes WebGoat as an interactive teaching environment for web application security.

openness.note: WebGoat is an OWASP project with public project pages and source-code access through OWASP/GitHub links.

depth.note: It lets developers test common vulnerabilities found in Java-based applications and popular open source components.

accessibility.note: WebGoat is powerful for developers, but it requires local setup and security care, so it is less beginner-friendly.

calm.note: It is a focused lab project, not a social or feed-driven learning platform.

economical.note: OWASP provides the WebGoat project as a public learning project rather than a paid course.

products.description: An intentionally vulnerable OWASP training application for practicing web application security in a safe, permissioned lab context.

products.name: CYBER.ORG Curricula

educational.note: CYBER.ORG offers K-12 cybersecurity lessons covering cyber literacy, security basics, coding, AI, networking and more.

openness.note: The course library is available at no cost to K-12 educators, but it is not simply open public-domain courseware.

depth.note: The site describes modular curriculum, professional development, standards mapping, range practice and career pathway support.

accessibility.note: Materials are written by educators, Chromebook-compatible and designed for first-time cybersecurity instructors.

calm.note: The resource is curriculum- and classroom-based rather than a social learning feed.

economical.note: CYBER.ORG describes no-cost or low-cost solutions, with complete course library access at no cost to K-12 educators.

products.description: A K-12 cybersecurity education hub with curriculum, educator support, professional development and simulated cyber practice resources.

products.name: NICE Cybersecurity Career Pathway Resources

educational.note: NIST NICE curates cybersecurity career pathway tools, educational pathways, certification pathways and related learning resources.

openness.note: The page is a public NIST resource, though it links to a mix of public, commercial and third-party tools without NIST endorsement.

depth.note: The resource connects career tools, educational pathways, certification pathways and NICE Framework-aligned work-role information.

accessibility.note: It is useful for orientation, but it is a directory and framework resource rather than a step-by-step course.

calm.note: The NIST page is a static public-interest reference rather than an engagement-optimized learning platform.

economical.note: The NIST career-pathway resource is publicly accessible online at no cost.

products.description: A public NIST orientation hub for understanding cybersecurity career paths, work roles, education routes and certification pathways.

products.name: Northstar Digital Literacy

educational.note: LINCS describes Northstar as standards-based digital literacy assessments and learning modules for adult learners.

openness.note: LINCS lists an open-access version of the Northstar assessments, while full organization features are separate.

depth.note: The listed modules cover basic computer skills, internet, operating systems, email, social media, office tools and information literacy.

accessibility.note: LINCS says the lessons are simple to understand and navigate and were designed for adult basic-skills learners.

calm.note: Northstar is assessment- and module-based rather than a feed or entertainment-driven learning platform.

economical.note: LINCS identifies an open-access assessment version, though subscribing organizations can add reporting and administration features.

products.description: A practical assessment-and-lessons pathway for adults building basic computer, internet, email, office and information-literacy skills.

products.name: Learn My Way

educational.note: Good Things describes Learn My Way as a free online learning platform for people developing digital skills.

openness.note: The platform is freely usable for learners, but the courseware is provided by Good Things rather than open-source community content.

depth.note: Good Things positions it around starter digital skills, confidence and guided support rather than advanced technical depth.

accessibility.note: Good Things provides guidance for digital champions to help new learners get started, register and track progress.

calm.note: Learn My Way is built around guided self-paced digital-skills topics rather than social feeds or competitive gamification.

economical.note: Good Things explicitly calls Learn My Way a free learning resource and free online learning platform.

products.description: A UK digital-inclusion learning platform for beginners building confidence with devices, online communication and everyday digital tasks.

products.name: DataBasic

educational.note: DataBasic describes beginner-friendly web tools that introduce concepts for working with data and telling stories with it.

openness.note: The site describes DataBasic as a free and open-source project with public software development links.
