depth.note: The suite covers text counting, CSV exploration, document comparison, network analysis and facilitation activities.

accessibility.note: DataBasic says its tools support screen readers and are designed for beginners who may not know technical terminology.

calm.note: Each tool focuses on one task and is designed for learning, not speed, feeds or engagement loops.

economical.note: DataBasic identifies itself as a free project supported by philanthropic and academic funding.

products.description: A set of simple, open tools and activities that help beginners explore text, spreadsheets and networks without needing to code.

products.name: Webwise

educational.note: Webwise provides information, advice and resources for schools, families and young people on online safety and digital citizenship.

openness.note: The site offers public resources and teacher materials, though it is a managed national awareness centre rather than open courseware.

depth.note: Its resource areas cover teachers, parents, youth, classroom videos, cyberbullying, AI safety and Safer Internet Day materials.

accessibility.note: Webwise separates resources for parents, teachers and youth and includes school-facing and family-facing entry points.

calm.note: The resource is structured around guidance, classroom resources and helplines rather than an attention-driven content feed.

economical.note: Webwise labels its teaching resources as free and publishes online safety guidance publicly.

products.description: Ireland's public online-safety and digital-citizenship hub for schools, families and young people.

products.name: eSafety Classroom Resources

educational.note: The eSafety Commissioner describes classroom resources designed to help educators teach online-safety lessons.

openness.note: The classroom-resource library is public government material, with resources listed directly on the eSafety website.

depth.note: The page links many topic areas including misinformation, digital reputation, cyberbullying, privacy, consent, AI and online-safety frameworks.

accessibility.note: Resources are organized for educators, students and schools, with classroom posters, videos, toolkits and easy-read material.

calm.note: The site emphasizes structured guidance and education rather than social participation or gamified competition.

economical.note: The eSafety classroom resources are published online by a public regulator with no listed learner fee.

products.description: A public regulator's library of classroom online-safety, cyberbullying, misinformation, privacy and digital-wellbeing resources.

products.name: NAMLE Resources
products.brand: National Association for Media Literacy Education

educational.note: NAMLE frames its resources around accessing, analyzing, evaluating, creating and acting using all forms of communication.

openness.note: NAMLE publishes free public resources and offers free membership, while some events and partner channels sit outside pure open access.

depth.note: The resource hub includes media literacy definitions, core principles, key questions, AI literacy, youth-led basics and journal links.

accessibility.note: The hub provides a plain public entry point, though much of the value is organized for educators and media-literacy practitioners.

calm.note: NAMLE is an educational nonprofit resource hub rather than a feed-first or credential-pressure learning platform.

economical.note: The public resources are free to browse and NAMLE lists free membership, though it also runs events, shops and partner programs.

products.description: A nonprofit hub for media-literacy definitions, principles, educator resources, AI-literacy work and youth-facing critical media basics.

products.name: MisinfoDay

educational.note: The UW Center for an Informed Public describes MisinfoDay as helping students, teachers and librarians navigate complex information environments.

openness.note: MisinfoDay offers a free resource library for educators and publishes new curricular resources annually.

depth.note: The program includes campus events, classroom resources, a community toolkit and media mentorship projects.

accessibility.note: The resource library and classroom event model are educator-friendly, but the strongest path is through school or library facilitation.

calm.note: MisinfoDay is built as curriculum and event programming, not a scrolling news or social platform.

economical.note: The MisinfoDay page describes its year-round resource library as free lessons and resources for educators.

products.description: A media-literacy program and free resource library for teaching students how to evaluate information and misinformation.

products.name: Digital literacy for children: 10 things you need to know

educational.note: UNICEF explains digital literacy for children as knowledge, skills and attitudes for safety and empowerment in a digital world.

openness.note: The report page and downloadable PDF are publicly available from UNICEF Innocenti.

depth.note: The publication covers frameworks, children's rights, assessment, context, implementation barriers and global coordination gaps.

accessibility.note: It is concise and public, but it is a policy/research brief rather than a hands-on course for a beginner learner.

calm.note: The resource is a static research brief with no feeds, ads or engagement mechanics.

economical.note: UNICEF makes the publication available online and as a PDF download at no cost.

products.description: A concise UNICEF research brief for understanding what children's digital literacy should include beyond basic technical skills.

products.name: TryHackMe

educational.note: TryHackMe describes itself as browser-based, hands-on cybersecurity training with labs, walkthroughs and challenges.

openness.note: Hundreds of rooms are free, but full paths, simulations, certificates and unlimited AttackBox time require paid tiers.

depth.note: The free-room page lists beginner through advanced labs and says premium unlocks full learning paths and real-world network simulations.

accessibility.note: TryHackMe runs in the browser and includes beginner-friendly free rooms, but technical security labs still require comfort with hands-on tools.

calm.note: The platform is gamified and challenge-oriented, which can be motivating but less calm than static curriculum.

economical.note: TryHackMe lists 650+ free rooms, while full access requires Premium or Max.

products.description: A mainstream hands-on cybersecurity platform with many free browser-based rooms and paid paths for deeper training.

products.name: HTB Academy

educational.note: HTB Academy describes guided cybersecurity training with interactive, hands-on practice and job or skill paths.

openness.note: The FAQ says some Fundamental modules can be started free, but Easy, Medium and Hard modules require cubes or subscription plans.

depth.note: The catalogue includes many offensive, defensive and general modules, from fundamentals to hard topics and certification paths.

accessibility.note: The FAQ says Academy is browser-based and beginner-friendly for Fundamental and Easy modules, but the content is technical and account-based.

calm.note: HTB Academy is structured around modules and guided paths, though certification and cyber challenge framing can add pressure.

economical.note: The FAQ says users get some free cubes and free Tier 0 modules, but broader access requires purchased cubes or subscriptions.

products.description: A deep guided cybersecurity academy with browser-based labs, skill paths and certifications, balanced by a paid cube/subscription model.

products.name: Senior Planet

educational.note: Senior Planet offers live and online classes that include practical technology topics such as AI, online shopping and digital payments.

openness.note: The site publishes a large public schedule and lets users sign up for free, though it is a managed program rather than open courseware.

depth.note: Senior Planet has broad everyday technology coverage, but most sessions are introductory rather than technical deep dives.

accessibility.note: Senior Planet is explicitly designed for people aged 60 and older and offers online, in-person and on-demand learning routes.

calm.note: The program is class- and community-based, with supportive trainers and no feed-like learning pressure.

economical.note: Senior Planet labels its technology training and on-demand learning as free.

products.description: A free technology-learning and community program built for older adults who want practical help with digital life.

products.name: Cyber-Seniors

educational.note: Cyber-Seniors provides technology support and training for older adults, including webinars on privacy, AI scams and online trust.

openness.note: Cyber-Seniors lists free programs, services and webinars publicly, while some program delivery is organized through partners.

depth.note: The program focuses on practical help and introductory technology confidence rather than advanced technical curriculum.

accessibility.note: The site offers toll-free support, multiple time zones, webinars and English, French and Spanish entry points.

calm.note: Its intergenerational volunteer model and drop-in support are oriented around help and confidence rather than engagement mechanics.

economical.note: Cyber-Seniors describes its technology support and training as free and provides a toll-free help line.

products.description: Free technology support, webinars and volunteer mentoring for older adults who want safer, more confident digital lives.

products.name: Digital Skills Library

educational.note: The Digital Skills Library is an educator-curated repository for adult learners' personal, civic, educational and career digital skills.

openness.note: The library presents itself as an open repository of free learning resources with crowdsourced contributions.

depth.note: Resources are searchable by domain, skill, format and library source, and align to the BRIDGES Digital Resilience Toolkit.

accessibility.note: It is designed for adult learners and digital navigators, with filters for videos, PDFs, lessons, simulations and tutorials.

calm.note: The library is a searchable resource repository rather than a social, gamified or feed-driven platform.

economical.note: The site describes the library as a repository of free learning resources.

products.description: An open repository of free adult digital-skills learning resources curated for digital navigators, instructors and learners.

products.name: ProjectEVOLVE

educational.note: ProjectEVOLVE resources hundreds of Education for a Connected World statements with activities, outcomes and supporting materials.

openness.note: SWGfL describes ProjectEVOLVE as a free online-safety digital education toolkit, though school accounts and EDU training are structured services.

depth.note: The toolkit covers online identity, relationships, bullying, health, privacy, security, copyright and managing online information.

accessibility.note: Educators can search by keyword, strand, key stage, age and theme to customize resources for learners.

calm.note: ProjectEVOLVE emphasizes discussion, reflection and non-moralising education rather than scare tactics or engagement loops.

economical.note: SWGfL repeatedly describes ProjectEVOLVE as free to use.

products.description: A free UK online-safety and digital-education toolkit that turns the Education for a Connected World framework into classroom resources.

products.name: DigComp 3.0

educational.note: DigComp 3.0 describes knowledge, skills and attitudes needed for digital competence in daily life, society, work and learning.

openness.note: The European Commission JRC publication page provides the official public framework and downloadable publication metadata.

depth.note: The fifth edition adds granular learning outcomes and integrates AI across the digital competence framework.

accessibility.note: It is a formal framework for educators, governments and organizations, so it is less accessible than a learner-facing course.

calm.note: DigComp is a static public reference framework with no ads, feeds or gamified pressure.

economical.note: The official JRC publication is publicly accessible online at no cost.

products.description: The European Commission's digital-competence framework for mapping the knowledge, skills and attitudes needed for digital life.

products.name: Cisco Networking Academy Digital Literacy

educational.note: Cisco Networking Academy describes digital-literacy courses for practical digital skills, devices and digital safety.

openness.note: Cisco offers free online courses, but the learning collection is account-based and institutionally managed rather than open courseware.

depth.note: The digital-literacy collection covers computer and mobile device use, online navigation, digital content and digital safety.

accessibility.note: The courses are positioned for basic skills and confidence, with self-paced and instructor-led options.

calm.note: The course collection is structured around skills and career pathways, with less social-feed pressure than entertainment learning platforms.

economical.note: Cisco describes Skills for All and digital-literacy learning as free online tech courses.

products.description: A Cisco-backed collection of free beginner digital-literacy courses covering devices, online tools, collaboration and digital safety.

products.name: IBM SkillsBuild

educational.note: IBM SkillsBuild offers job skills, courses and credentials for adult learners, students, educators and communities.

openness.note: IBM makes the training free, but it is account-based corporate learning rather than open-source or open-licensed courseware.

depth.note: Adult learner pathways include cybersecurity, data, information technology, IT project management and web development.

accessibility.note: The adult-learner page says the program helps people gain foundational entry-level tech skills and credentials at no cost.

calm.note: SkillsBuild is structured around pathways and credentials, helpful for careers but more achievement-oriented than a quiet reference library.

economical.note: IBM states that SkillsBuild courses, resources and credentials are free and at no cost.

products.description: A free IBM learning platform for foundational tech, workplace skills, job pathways and digital credentials.

products.name: Project Look Sharp

educational.note: Project Look Sharp provides media-literacy lessons, materials and professional development for inquiry-based media analysis.

openness.note: The site highlights free materials, starter kits, handouts and media decoding demonstrations.

depth.note: It includes lessons across AI, social media, technology, civics, history and many grade levels.

accessibility.note: Resources are searchable by age or grade level and offer role-specific pathways for teachers, librarians and teacher educators.

calm.note: The approach emphasizes inquiry, reflection and evidence-based analysis rather than alarmist media-safety messaging.

economical.note: Project Look Sharp publishes free materials and lesson resources for educators.

products.description: A media-literacy education hub with free inquiry-based lessons, decoding tools and professional resources for teachers and librarians.

products.name: Social Media TestDrive
products.brand: Cornell Social Media Lab / Common Sense Education

educational.note: Social Media TestDrive teaches digital citizenship through simulated social-media dilemmas and experiential learning.

openness.note: Modules are publicly available to try, with educator and parent pathways, though the platform is not a general open repository.

depth.note: Modules cover privacy, online identity, cyberbullying and other digital citizenship concepts for young social-media users.

accessibility.note: The site targets middle-school-aged youth and can be used individually, in pairs, in guided groups, or at home.

calm.note: It uses contained simulations rather than real social feeds and says it does not collect personal identifying information.

economical.note: The platform's modules are publicly accessible online and positioned for educators, parents and youth without a listed fee.

products.description: A simulated social-media learning environment where young people can practice privacy, identity and digital citizenship choices safely.

products.name: Digital Citizenship+ Resource Platform
products.brand: Berkman Klein Center Youth and Media

educational.note: Harvard's Berkman Klein Center describes DCRP as learning experiences and educational resources for youth's digitally connected lives.

openness.note: DCRP tools are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 unless otherwise specified.

depth.note: The platform spans 17 digital-life areas including AI, data, digital economy, information quality, privacy, safety and security.

accessibility.note: It includes school, family and individual youth activities, plus some translated tools, but the resource platform can feel educator-oriented.

calm.note: DCRP is a public educational resource platform, not a commercial feed or gamified credential platform.

economical.note: The resources are publicly available and Creative Commons-licensed, supporting no-cost reuse.

products.description: A Creative Commons resource platform for teaching youth about digital citizenship, privacy, safety, media literacy and digital rights.

products.name: InformationLiteracy.gov
products.brand: Institute of Museum and Library Services

educational.note: The federal site defines information literacy as skills to find, understand, evaluate and share information, with resources for communities, classrooms and home use.

openness.note: InformationLiteracy.gov is an official U.S. government resource hub with public pages for AI, digital, financial, health and science literacy.

depth.note: IMLS describes the initiative as covering successful practices, tools and programs across digital, financial, health and other information-literacy areas.

accessibility.note: The site is geared toward library and museum professionals, which is useful for programs but less direct than a learner-first course.

calm.note: The hub emphasizes practical community education and trusted information skills rather than commercial engagement mechanics.

economical.note: The public federal resource hub is freely accessible online.

products.description: A U.S. federal hub for library, museum and community professionals teaching information, digital, AI, financial, health and science literacy.

products.name: Education for a Connected World

educational.note: GOV.UK describes the framework as equipping children and young people for digital life.

openness.note: The framework is published on GOV.UK with an open public PDF and Crown copyright / Open Government Licence notice.

depth.note: The page says the framework describes digital knowledge and skills children should develop at different ages and stages.

accessibility.note: The main document is a 65-page PDF, and GOV.UK notes it may not be suitable for all assistive-technology users.

calm.note: The framework supports skills and development across online life rather than relying on fear-based safety messaging.

economical.note: The framework is publicly downloadable from GOV.UK at no listed cost.

products.description: A UK public framework describing the digital knowledge and skills children and young people should build across age bands.

products.name: Making Sense of Media

educational.note: Ofcom describes Making Sense of Media as a programme to improve the media literacy of UK adults and children.

openness.note: Ofcom publishes research, delivery plans, best-practice principles and evaluation tools through the public programme page.

depth.note: The programme includes research into adult and child media habits, critical understanding, pilots, campaigns and platform-design principles.

accessibility.note: The page is strongest for stakeholders and program designers; Ofcom lists pilots for older adults, disabled people, children and financially disadvantaged communities.

calm.note: Ofcom says it takes a 'what works' evidence and action-research approach to improving media literacy knowledge and skills.

economical.note: Ofcom's research and toolkit materials are publicly available from the regulator's website.

products.description: Ofcom's media-literacy research and practice programme for UK adults, children, educators, platforms and community stakeholders.

products.name: Media Literacy Now Resource Library

educational.note: Media Literacy Now says the library helps classrooms, homes, communities and constituents advocate for media literacy education.

openness.note: The resource library is publicly browseable and lists categories for educators, parents, families, advocacy tools and policy reports.

depth.note: The site lists 216 documents and includes AI literacy, digital wellbeing, social-media literacy, curriculum and policy resources.

accessibility.note: The library is searchable and browsable by audience and topic, though some linked resources lead to external providers.

calm.note: Media Literacy Now frames the work around education, health, well-being, economic participation and citizenship.

economical.note: The library itself is public; some third-party resources it links may have their own access terms.

products.description: A media-literacy advocacy and resource library for families, educators, school leaders and community policy work.

products.name: Media Literacy Education in Libraries for Adult Audiences

educational.note: ALA says the project supports libraries in improving adult media literacy skills in their communities.

openness.note: ALA publishes free media literacy resources, guides and webinars on the project page.

depth.note: The page includes practitioner guides, program models, webinars on AI, data security, algorithms, attention economy and misinformation.

accessibility.note: The resources are designed for library workers to teach adult patrons, so they are practical but indirect for solo learners.

calm.note: The project focuses on adult community learning, online information assessment and informed decision-making.

economical.note: ALA labels the project guides and resource downloads as free.

products.description: Free ALA program models, practitioner guides and webinars for libraries teaching adults how online information systems work.

products.name: AT&T Connected Learning Resources

educational.note: AT&T says Connected Learning provides computers, internet connectivity, online learning, and digital skills and literacy training.

openness.note: The public page links to digital literacy courses, parenting resources, The Achievery and Connected Learning Centers, but it is a corporate hub.

depth.note: The hub covers digital literacy courses, parenting resources, K-12 learning activities, community centers, free computers and low-cost internet pathways.

accessibility.note: AT&T describes Connected Learning Centers across the country that provide free internet, computers, training and mentoring through nonprofits.

calm.note: The hub is service-oriented but sits inside a large telecom brand's corporate responsibility site.

economical.note: The page describes free community resources, free computer distribution through nonprofits and low-cost internet service for eligible households.

products.description: A corporate digital-inclusion hub linking digital literacy courses, family resources, connected-learning centers and low-cost access programs.

products.name: AT&T ScreenReady

educational.note: ScreenReady provides resources, tips and tools for technology confidence, healthy digital habits and participation in a connected world.

openness.note: The public site offers sections for parents and caregivers, kids and teens, teachers and educators, adults and seniors, but remains corporate-branded.

depth.note: ScreenReady links app guides, digital citizenship courses, online safety resources and standards-aligned learning activities.

accessibility.note: The resource pathways are split by life stage and role, including parents, youth, teachers, adults and seniors.

calm.note: The site frames screen use around balanced and safe experiences rather than sensational warnings.

economical.note: ScreenReady's resource pages are publicly accessible online at no listed cost.

products.description: A family and educator resource hub for healthy digital habits, online safety, digital citizenship and age-based screen guidance.

products.name: Digital Navigator Program Toolkit

educational.note: NDIA says the toolkit guides organizations in setting up and managing digital navigator programs.

openness.note: The 2025 toolkit is published as a public NDIA resource with a download link.

depth.note: NDIA says the toolkit draws on experience training, supporting and learning from hundreds of digital navigators and programs.

accessibility.note: The toolkit is meant for programs rather than direct learners, so it is most useful to libraries, nonprofits and local digital-equity teams.

calm.note: The resource emphasizes practical best practices for sustainable navigator programs and local support.

economical.note: The toolkit is listed as a downloadable public NDIA resource.

products.description: A practical toolkit for organizations building digital navigator services that help people with devices, connectivity and digital skills.

products.name: Cyber Readiness Program

educational.note: CRI describes the program as a free, self-paced way for SMBs to build practical cybersecurity habits and cyber-readiness culture.

openness.note: The program is public and free, though participants use CRI's program signup and course environment.

depth.note: The program covers passwords and multifactor authentication, software updates, phishing, and secure storage and sharing.

accessibility.note: CRI says the online program is designed for SMBs of all sizes and technical abilities with no technical background required.

calm.note: The program focuses on simple behavior changes, policies, checklists and workforce training rather than threat hype.

economical.note: CRI lists the program as free with no cost for any user.

products.description: A free, self-paced cybersecurity readiness program for small and medium-sized businesses and their workers.

products.name: Google News Initiative Training Center

educational.note: Google News Initiative says its trainings sharpen skills and teach current best practices through self-paced lessons and workshops.

openness.note: The training catalogue is publicly browseable, but it is hosted by Google and partly oriented toward publishers and journalists.

depth.note: The training filters include digital reporting skills, misinformation, audience development, revenue and product-building tracks.

products.description: A weekly classroom-ready news-literacy digest for teaching misinformation, AI, journalism and press-freedom topics as they arise.

products.name: Citizen Evidence Lab

educational.note: Citizen Evidence Lab shares guides to digital investigative methods for human-rights research, including verification and case studies.

openness.note: The online resource is publicly available and managed by Amnesty International's Evidence Lab.

depth.note: Its guides and case studies cover open-source information, video and photo verification, remote sensing and weapons analysis.

accessibility.note: The material supports researchers, investigators, students and journalists, but assumes interest in human-rights investigation methods.

calm.note: The resource is methodical and case-study based, though human-rights evidence can involve distressing contexts.

economical.note: The Evidence Lab materials are available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A public-interest verification resource for learning how open-source images, video, maps and data can support human-rights investigations.

products.name: The Journalist's Resource

educational.note: The Journalist's Resource curates, summarizes and contextualizes research on public-policy topics for journalists and the public.

openness.note: The project publishes public explainers and research summaries through Harvard Kennedy School's Shorenstein Center.

depth.note: It helps readers interpret academic evidence behind news topics rather than relying only on headlines or opinion.

accessibility.note: The site is written to make academic research accessible for people reporting on or trying to understand the news.

calm.note: The format favors explainers and research context rather than breaking-news feeds.

economical.note: The resource is publicly available online without a listed subscription fee.

products.description: Research-literacy support for journalists, students and readers who want to understand public-policy evidence behind the news.

products.name: Privacy International Data Protection Guide

educational.note: Privacy International's guide explains data-protection concepts and how to analyze common provisions in data-protection law.

openness.note: The guide is publicly available and offered in English and Spanish.

depth.note: It is built for policy engagement and legal analysis, so it goes deeper than basic consumer privacy checklists.

accessibility.note: The material is useful for organizations and advocates but is more policy-heavy than beginner privacy guidance.

calm.note: The guide is analytical and rights-focused rather than a scare-driven privacy product page.

economical.note: Privacy International publishes the guide online without a listed fee.

products.description: A deeper policy-literacy guide for understanding data-protection laws, rights and governance rather than only personal privacy tips.

products.name: Me and My Shadow

educational.note: Me and My Shadow helps people understand data traces, tracking and the data industry.

openness.note: Tactical Tech publishes the privacy resource publicly online.

depth.note: Trace My Shadow turns device and service choices into concrete examples of digital traces and mitigation steps.

accessibility.note: The resource is designed for non-specialists who want to see and reduce their digital footprints.

calm.note: It explains tracking and control steps, though the topic can still feel unsettling for privacy beginners.

economical.note: The site and Trace My Shadow tool are publicly accessible without a listed fee.

products.description: A Tactical Tech privacy-literacy resource that makes digital traces, tracking and data-industry habits visible to ordinary users.

products.name: Novice to Know-How

educational.note: The beginner pathway teaches digital preservation concepts, actions and workflows for organizations handling digital content.

openness.note: The course is provided through DPC's learning platform and has registration/cohort mechanics rather than being a fully open static text.

depth.note: The course covers preservation issues, workflows, tool demos, video, text and quizzes, with learners typically taking two to three days.

accessibility.note: It is aimed at beginners in digital preservation, but the audience is mainly archives and information-management practitioners.

calm.note: The self-paced training emphasizes practical workflows and free, easy-to-use options rather than urgent vendor migration.

economical.note: DPC materials describe access as free for all learners, with course places managed through the DPC platform.

products.description: A beginner digital-preservation pathway for people responsible for keeping files, records and collections usable over time.

products.name: NonprofitReady

educational.note: NonprofitReady offers free courses, certificates, videos and guides for nonprofit skills such as fundraising, grantwriting and leadership.

openness.note: The training is free to learners, but it is hosted on a proprietary course platform rather than an open curriculum repository.

depth.note: The platform describes more than 600 learning resources for nonprofit professionals, board members and volunteers.

accessibility.note: Courses are online and aimed at people at every stage of a nonprofit career, though an account is required for participation.

calm.note: The site is skills-focused, but certificates and course-platform structure add more career signaling than a simple reference library.

economical.note: NonprofitReady says its courses and certificate programs are 100% free.

products.description: A free professional-learning hub for people building nonprofit, volunteer, grantwriting and public-good organizational skills.

products.name: AI Incident Database

educational.note: AI Incident Database indexes real-world AI harms and near harms so learners can study failures rather than only capabilities.

openness.note: The database is publicly searchable and collects incident reports for shared learning about AI failures.

depth.note: Partnership on AI describes AIID as collecting more than 1,200 reports of intelligent systems causing real-world problems.

accessibility.note: It is useful for AI ethics and policy learners, but incident databases require interpretation and context.

calm.note: The resource is evidence-oriented, though studying harms and failures can be less calming than basic AI tutorials.

economical.note: The AI Incident Database is publicly accessible online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A public AI-literacy database for learning from real-world AI failures, harms and near misses.

products.name: MIT AI Risk Repository

educational.note: MIT AI Risk Repository provides data and frameworks to help identify, prioritize and manage AI risks.

openness.note: The initiative publishes public tools including risk, incident, mitigation and governance views.

depth.note: MIT's incident tracker classifies more than 1,400 real-world AI incidents by risk, cause, harm, severity and other dimensions.

accessibility.note: The repository is powerful for researchers and governance learners, but is more technical than beginner AI-literacy lessons.

calm.note: It is structured as a risk-analysis tool, which is clearer than hype but still centered on harms and governance concerns.

economical.note: The repository and incident tracker are publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A deeper AI-risk literacy tool for understanding categories of AI harm, mitigation and governance evidence.

products.name: Microsoft Accessibility Fundamentals

educational.note: Microsoft's accessibility fundamentals path introduces accessibility concepts, assistive technologies and web accessibility principles.

openness.note: The learning path is free on Microsoft Learn, though it sits inside Microsoft's proprietary learning ecosystem.

depth.note: The path covers core definitions, assistive technology and web accessibility guidelines rather than advanced auditing practice.

accessibility.note: Microsoft frames the path as a beginner-friendly way to understand why technology should be accessible to everyone.

calm.note: The modular Microsoft Learn format is self-paced and structured rather than feed-driven.

economical.note: Microsoft announced the updated Accessibility Fundamentals learning path as free for all on Microsoft Learn.

products.description: A beginner accessibility learning path for people who want a structured introduction inside Microsoft Learn.

products.name: Section508.gov Accessibility Training

educational.note: Section508.gov training is intended to improve understanding of IT accessibility, Section 508 law and accessible digital content.

openness.note: The training hub is public U.S. government accessibility guidance.

depth.note: The hub includes online training courses, a video library, on-demand webinars and additional training resources.

accessibility.note: The content is practical for people producing digital tools and content, though U.S. federal compliance language can be specialized.

calm.note: The training library is standards-oriented and self-paced rather than commercial or gamified.

economical.note: Section508.gov training materials are publicly available online.

products.description: A U.S. public-sector accessibility training hub for learning Section 508, accessible content and IT accessibility practice.

products.name: Deque University

educational.note: Deque University provides self-guided accessibility courses for web, documents and mobile content.

openness.note: The curriculum is proprietary and subscription-based for many learners, with scholarships for qualifying disabled learners.

depth.note: Deque describes an extensive curriculum with detailed courses, examples and certification preparation.

accessibility.note: Self-paced courses are flexible, but full access generally depends on subscription or scholarship eligibility.

calm.note: The course library is self-paced and reference-like rather than a feed, but professional certification goals may add pressure.

economical.note: Deque offers free access for individuals with disabilities, while other learners may need paid subscription access.

products.description: A deep professional accessibility course library, with a real access caveat: many learners face paid access unless scholarship-eligible.

products.name: Be Connected

educational.note: Be Connected builds confidence, digital skills and online safety for older Australians through free online resources and classes.

openness.note: The resource is an Australian government initiative with free online learning resources.

depth.note: It combines self-paced online topics with a community network, but is focused on older-adult digital confidence rather than advanced training.

accessibility.note: The program is designed for people over 50 and includes online learning plus community organizations running free computer classes.

calm.note: The tone centers confidence, safety and community support for older learners.

economical.note: Be Connected states that learners can access free learning resources online or join free computer classes.

products.description: A government-backed older-adult digital confidence program, especially useful as a model for calm beginner online-safety support.

products.name: Data Governance Workbook

educational.note: The workbook helps nonprofits consider key questions for safe, ethical and effective data governance.

openness.note: The workbook is published as a public data.org resource from Stanford PACS Center on Philanthropy and Civil Society.

depth.note: Stanford's Digital Civil Society Lab work focuses on organizations, technology, policy and values in digitally dependent civil society.

accessibility.note: The resource is beginner-labeled but is aimed at nonprofit and civil-society data stewards more than casual learners.

calm.note: The workbook format supports reflective planning rather than reactive data-risk alerts.

economical.note: The workbook is available as a public resource online.

products.description: A practical data-governance workbook for nonprofits and civil-society groups learning to steward digital data responsibly.

products.name: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education

educational.note: The course teaches practical computing tools often omitted from CS classes, including shell, editors, version control and debugging.

openness.note: Lecture notes and videos are publicly available, and the course website repository accepts contributions.

depth.note: The 2026 lectures include command line, shell tools, data wrangling, editors, Git, debugging, profiling and security topics.

accessibility.note: The material is free and well documented, but assumes comfort with technical computing and command-line tools.

calm.note: The resource is lecture-note based and self-paced rather than gamified or credential-driven.

economical.note: The course materials are publicly accessible online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A free MIT-born course for the everyday developer tools that make digital work safer and less mysterious.

products.name: Open Source Society University Computer Science

educational.note: OSSU curates a self-taught computer science curriculum from free learning resources.

openness.note: The curriculum is maintained openly on GitHub under the Open Source Society University organization.

depth.note: The curriculum spans core CS, advanced CS, applications, projects and community guidance.

accessibility.note: It is free but ambitious and self-directed, so beginners need persistence and outside support.

calm.note: The roadmap is structured but large, which can be motivating for some learners and overwhelming for others.

economical.note: OSSU describes itself as a path to a free self-taught education in computer science.

products.description: A community-curated, open roadmap for learners who want a free self-study path through computer science.

products.name: OverTheWire

educational.note: OverTheWire wargames help learners practice security concepts through hands-on challenges.

openness.note: The wargames are publicly available community resources, though not a formal open curriculum.

depth.note: The Bandit track teaches command-line and security basics before harder wargames.

accessibility.note: Bandit is aimed at absolute beginners, but learners still need comfort with terminals and puzzle-based self-study.

calm.note: The wargame style is useful practice but less calm than a guided course because learners progress by solving challenges.

economical.note: OverTheWire wargames are available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A hands-on security wargame site that turns command-line and security basics into practical puzzles.

products.name: OpenSecurityTraining2

educational.note: OpenSecurityTraining2 provides self-paced classes for high-skill cybersecurity topics.

openness.note: The site says anyone can freely take its self-paced classes at any time.

depth.note: The course catalog includes multi-class learning paths and advanced topics such as firmware, fuzzing, debugging and exploitation.

accessibility.note: The content is free but aimed at technical security learners rather than casual digital-safety beginners.

calm.note: It is self-paced and open access, but advanced security topics can be demanding.

economical.note: OpenSecurityTraining2 says its classes are freely available.

products.description: A deep open-access cybersecurity training library for learners ready to move beyond basic awareness into technical security practice.

products.name: OpenSSF Training

educational.note: OpenSSF training teaches secure software development and security concepts for people building software.

openness.note: OpenSSF publishes training and course content, including open course materials maintained through the foundation.

depth.note: The Developing Secure Software course covers hardened software, vulnerability handling and open-source software security basics.

accessibility.note: The flagship course is online and self-paced, but assumes interest in software development.

calm.note: The course is practical and self-paced rather than feed-driven or fear-based.

economical.note: OpenSSF says both the Developing Secure Software course and certificate of completion are free.

products.description: Free secure-software training for learners who want to connect digital literacy with safer software practice.

products.name: CISA Learning

educational.note: CISA Learning offers no-cost online cybersecurity training on topics such as cloud security, malware analysis and risk management.

openness.note: The training is provided as a public CISA/NICCS resource.

depth.note: CISA Learning replaces and expands access to many no-cost cybersecurity courses for government staff, veterans and external partners.

accessibility.note: The courses are no-cost online training, though account access and eligibility details may vary by learner group.

calm.note: The resource is workforce-oriented and practical rather than consumer-alarm content.

economical.note: CISA describes the training as no-cost online cybersecurity training.

products.description: A public U.S. cybersecurity training platform for people moving from general awareness into workforce-level cyber skills.

products.name: Cybrary

educational.note: Cybrary offers cybersecurity and IT training, including free foundational courses and career paths.

openness.note: Free access exists, but Cybrary is a proprietary commercial platform with paid Insider Pro and Teams tiers.

depth.note: Cybrary says it offers foundational courses, paths and labs for cybersecurity learners and professionals.

accessibility.note: Learners can start for free, but account signup and paid-course boundaries make it less open than public or nonprofit resources.

calm.note: Career-path and certification framing can be useful, but it is more pressure-oriented than a static public guide.

economical.note: Cybrary provides some free content, while fuller access and team training are commercial.

products.description: A mainstream cybersecurity training platform with real free entry points and an honest proprietary/paywall tradeoff.

products.name: Learn to Discern

educational.note: Learn to Discern teaches media and information-literacy skills for identifying disinformation and manipulative information.

openness.note: IREX publishes program information and curriculum materials online, though full implementation often happens through programs and partners.

depth.note: The curriculum covers habits, media literacy, misinformation, social media and information-consumption wellbeing.

accessibility.note: The materials are useful for educators and communities, but PDFs and program framing are less plug-and-play than a web course.

calm.note: The program explicitly includes digital-space participation without undermining wellbeing, dignity or humanity.

economical.note: The fact sheet and English curriculum are publicly accessible online.

products.description: A media-literacy curriculum and program model for building resilience to manipulative information and disinformation.

products.name: Calling Bullshit

educational.note: Calling Bullshit teaches data reasoning in a digital world and how to detect misleading use of data and evidence.

openness.note: The course website publishes the syllabus, readings, videos and FAQ publicly.

depth.note: The syllabus covers spotting bullshit, causality, statistical traps, big data, visualization, publication bias and refutation.

accessibility.note: The public course materials are approachable but still assume comfort with data, science and argument analysis.

calm.note: The tone is direct and memorable, with lecture materials rather than feed-driven outrage.

economical.note: The course website and lecture materials are publicly available online without a listed fee.

products.description: A public course on data reasoning, misinformation and misleading evidence, useful for people who want sharper BS detection.

products.name: Seeing Theory

educational.note: Seeing Theory uses interactive visualizations to make probability and statistics more accessible.

openness.note: The site remains publicly hosted, and the source code is available on GitHub.

depth.note: The project covers first-course statistics topics through explorable visualizations, though the repository notes it is no longer maintained.

accessibility.note: The project was created to make statistics more accessible through interactive D3 visualizations.

calm.note: The site is exploratory and self-paced rather than competitive or credential-driven.

economical.note: The visualizations are publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: An interactive visual statistics resource for building data intuition without starting from formulas alone.

products.name: Full Fact

educational.note: Full Fact publishes fact checks and a misinformation toolkit with practical verification guidance.

openness.note: Full Fact is a registered UK charity and nonprofit company, and publishes public fact checks and resources.

depth.note: Its toolkit covers practical topics such as spotting deepfake videos, AI audio and misleading conflict footage.

accessibility.note: The toolkit is written for public use, though the wider site is a fact-checking publisher rather than a course.

calm.note: Full Fact focuses on checking claims and explaining methods, but fact-check feeds can still feel current-events driven.

economical.note: Full Fact's toolkit and fact checks are publicly available online.

products.description: A nonprofit fact-checking and misinformation toolkit resource, especially useful for practical verification examples.

products.name: Snopes

educational.note: Snopes is a long-running fact-checking reference for internet rumors, myths and misinformation.

openness.note: Snopes publishes fact checks and methods publicly, though it is a commercial media site rather than an open curriculum.

depth.note: The Snopes-ing 101 collection gives how-tos from reporters and editors for fact-checking and internet research.

accessibility.note: The site is easy to search for specific claims, but ads and news-site packaging make it less calm than a course.

calm.note: Claim-by-claim fact-checking is useful but can pull users into a stream of current rumors and viral claims.

economical.note: Snopes fact checks and how-to collections are publicly readable online.

products.description: A widely recognized fact-checking reference that helps people research rumors, myths and viral misinformation.

products.name: PolitiFact

educational.note: PolitiFact publishes political fact checks and explains its Truth-O-Meter methodology for evaluating claims.

openness.note: PolitiFact states its principles as independence, transparency, fairness, thorough reporting and clear writing.

depth.note: Its methodology explains how claims are selected, researched, rated and corrected.

accessibility.note: Ratings and claim pages are easy to scan, though political fact-checking remains current-events heavy.

calm.note: It supports civic literacy, but the political-news context can be more activating than a classroom resource.

economical.note: PolitiFact fact checks and methodology pages are publicly available online.

products.description: A political fact-checking publisher with a public methodology, useful for learning how civic claims are evaluated.

products.name: USAFacts

educational.note: USAFacts makes U.S. government data easier to understand across topics such as economy, health, education and population.

openness.note: USAFacts describes itself as a not-for-profit, nonpartisan civic initiative using government data.

depth.note: Its data-methodology page explains why it relies on government data and how agency data is collected under laws and methodologies.

accessibility.note: USAFacts aims to make government data accessible through topic pages, explainers and standardized data presentations.

calm.note: The site emphasizes nonpartisan data context rather than partisan feeds or engagement loops.

economical.note: USAFacts public data pages are available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A civic data resource for learning from U.S. government statistics without starting from raw agency spreadsheets.

products.name: Ballotpedia

openness.note: Ballotpedia publishes public civic information, though it is professionally edited rather than an open public wiki.

depth.note: The site covers federal, state and local politics, elections and policy topics.

accessibility.note: The encyclopedia format makes political information searchable, but the volume of material can still be dense.

calm.note: Ballotpedia is reference-oriented rather than a social feed, though election content can still be politically activating.

economical.note: Ballotpedia pages are publicly readable online.

products.description: A searchable civic reference for U.S. elections, officials, ballot measures and policy background.

products.name: VOTE411

accessibility.note: The League of Women Voters describes VOTE411 as election information available in English and Spanish.

calm.note: The resource is task-focused and nonpartisan, helping voters answer concrete logistics questions.

products.name: Reading Wikipedia in the Classroom

openness.note: Wikimedia describes it as a flagship teacher training program with public modules and local implementations.

depth.note: The course connects Wikipedia learning to UNESCO media and information literacy concepts.

accessibility.note: It is aimed at educators and classroom settings, so it is less direct for casual individual learners.

calm.note: The program teaches critical evaluation of online knowledge rather than chasing breaking-news corrections.

economical.note: Program pages and course information are publicly available online.

products.description: A Wikimedia teacher-training program for turning Wikipedia use into media and information-literacy practice.

products.name: Wiki Education Dashboard

openness.note: The dashboard project publishes code openly and supports Wikipedia, Wikidata and Wikimedia education assignments.

depth.note: Instructor training explains how to organize assignments, monitor student work and teach with Wikipedia.

accessibility.note: It is powerful for classes and edit-a-thons, but depends on instructor setup and Wikipedia account workflows.

calm.note: The dashboard structures class editing work and progress tracking rather than social engagement loops.

economical.note: The dashboard and training pages are publicly accessible online.

products.description: A classroom and edit-a-thon tool for learning Wikipedia editing as public knowledge work.

products.name: UNICEF Online Safety

openness.note: The guidance is public child-protection and digital-education material from UNICEF.

depth.note: UNICEF covers child online safety, digital-literacy skills, platform safety, regulation and rights-based digital protection.

accessibility.note: The resource is written for parents, caregivers, professionals and institutions, though some pages are policy-oriented.

calm.note: UNICEF frames online safety around rights, literacy, safeguards and support instead of consumer security-product fear.

economical.note: UNICEF online safety and digital-education pages are publicly available.

products.description: Global public guidance on child online safety, digital literacy and rights-based protection in digital education.

products.name: UK Safer Internet Centre

openness.note: The resource is run by a partnership of UK charities and publishes public online-safety materials.

depth.note: The guide archive includes resources for schools, parents, young people, social media guides and safety checklists.

accessibility.note: European Safer Internet Centre descriptions note parent conversation starters, teacher toolkits, quizzes and youth resources.

calm.note: The centre frames safety as education and support for young people rather than product upsells.

economical.note: The online safety tips, advice and resource archive are publicly available online.

products.description: A UK online-safety hub for families, schools and young people, with resources that are still useful as general digital-safety examples.

products.name: Digital First Aid Kit

products.name: Holistic Security Manual

products.name: Video as Evidence Field Guide

economical.note: The guide is publicly available online for download and reading.

products.description: A field guide for learning how smartphone video can be captured, preserved and used responsibly as evidence.

products.name: HURIDOCS Resource Library

depth.note: Its resource library includes documentation, preservation, research, database and legal-advocacy materials.

accessibility.note: The resources are useful for civil-society documentation work, but more specialized than general digital-literacy courses.

calm.note: The materials emphasize preserving, organizing and protecting evidence, though the human-rights context can be intense.

products.name: LittleSis

products.name: OpenCorporates

products.name: USAspending.gov

products.name: CourtListener

products.name: Regulations.gov

depth.note: The platform includes dockets, agency documents, bulk data downloads and public-comment functions.

accessibility.note: Guidance pages explain how to access regulatory documents and engage in rulemaking, though the process remains formal.

calm.note: The site is task-oriented and procedural rather than attention-driven.
