openness.note: ODI publishes the canvas and interactive version publicly online.

depth.note: The canvas prompts users to ask practical questions about purpose, impacts, affected people and governance.

accessibility.note: The worksheet format makes data ethics concrete for teams without requiring a full academic course.

calm.note: The tool encourages reflection and practical risk management rather than alarm or hype.

economical.note: The Data Ethics Canvas is publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A practical worksheet for learning how to ask ethical questions before collecting, sharing or using data.

products.name: Principles for Digital Development

educational.note: The Digital Principles are living guidelines for people promoting sustainable and inclusive development with digital technology.

openness.note: The principles are community-driven and publicly documented for policymakers, practitioners and technologists.

depth.note: DIAL notes the principles were refreshed in 2024 after consultation with more than 300 stakeholders.

accessibility.note: The guidelines are approachable, though they are aimed at development programs and institutions rather than casual learners.

calm.note: The principles frame digital transformation through sustainability, inclusion and shared practice.

economical.note: The Digital Principles are publicly accessible online without a listed user fee.

products.description: Community-developed guidelines for learning how digital-development projects can be more inclusive, sustainable and reusable.

products.name: Responsible Data for Children

educational.note: RD4C provides guidance, tools and leadership for responsible handling of data for and about children.

openness.note: The initiative publishes public principles, resources, blog posts and tools online.

depth.note: UNICEF describes related work as fostering responsible data practices across industries, sectors and contexts for children.

accessibility.note: The site packages principles and resources for practitioners, though child-data governance is still a specialized topic.

calm.note: The resource frames child data governance through principles and practical tools.

economical.note: RD4C resources are publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A child-centered responsible-data resource for learning how digital systems can protect young people and their data.

products.name: Open Data Charter

educational.note: The charter explains open-data principles and why open data supports transparency, accountability and public services.

openness.note: The principles define open data as data made available for free use, reuse and redistribution by anyone.

depth.note: The six principles cover open by default, timeliness, usability, interoperability, governance and inclusive development.

accessibility.note: The informal explainer is readable, though implementation sections are aimed at governments and institutions.

calm.note: The charter presents norms and principles for public data rather than advocacy-only rhetoric.

economical.note: The Open Data Charter principles are publicly accessible online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A public principles resource for learning what makes government data usable, interoperable, accountable and open.

products.name: The Citizen Lab

educational.note: Citizen Lab investigates digital threats to democracy, human rights and global security in the digital ecosystem.

openness.note: Citizen Lab publishes public research reports and investigations online.

depth.note: Its work includes malware analysis, spyware investigations, digital espionage and threats to civil society.

accessibility.note: The reports are public, but many investigations require technical and human-rights context to interpret well.

calm.note: Citizen Lab uses evidence-heavy research, though the threats covered are serious and sometimes technical.

economical.note: Citizen Lab research is publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A research lab for learning how spyware, censorship, digital espionage and platform threats affect civil society.

products.name: Freedom on the Net

educational.note: Freedom on the Net helps learners compare internet freedom conditions through reports, country assessments, scores and maps.

openness.note: Freedom House publishes the report, map, methodology and downloadable data publicly online.

depth.note: The 2025 methodology assesses internet freedom in 72 countries using 21 indicators across access, content limits and rights violations.

accessibility.note: Maps and country reports help orientation, but the methodology and country assessments are long-form research.

calm.note: The annual report provides structured evidence and methodology rather than real-time outrage framing.

economical.note: Freedom on the Net materials are publicly accessible online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A global internet-freedom research project for learning how access, censorship, surveillance and online rights vary by country.

products.name: #KeepItOn

educational.note: #KeepItOn teaches internet-shutdown literacy through verified shutdown documentation, methodology and annual reporting.

openness.note: Access Now publishes a public dashboard, methodology, reports and downloadable STOP dataset for internet shutdowns.

depth.note: The 2026 campaign page links to 2016-2025 shutdown data and the 2025 global shutdowns report.

accessibility.note: Reports and dashboards make shutdown patterns visible, though the data is best for motivated civic learners.

calm.note: The campaign is rights-advocacy oriented, but it anchors claims in documented cases and methodology.

economical.note: #KeepItOn reports, dashboard and methodology are publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A global internet-shutdown evidence resource for learning how connectivity disruptions are documented and contested.

products.name: InVID-WeVerify Verification Plugin

educational.note: The plugin is designed to help journalists, fact-checkers and human-rights defenders verify videos and images.

openness.note: WeVerify documents the redesigned public plugin and its verification tools, though the browser-extension workflow is platform-bound.

depth.note: The tool combines contextual video information, reverse image search, metadata and other media-verification features.

accessibility.note: The plugin gives practitioners a single workflow, but media verification still requires judgment and training.

calm.note: The workflow supports evidence checking rather than viral debunking by reaction alone.

economical.note: The browser extension is publicly available through the Chrome Web Store without a listed user fee.

products.description: A browser-based verification toolkit for checking social video and image claims with reverse search, metadata and contextual tools.

products.name: TinEye Reverse Image Search

educational.note: TinEye helps learners check where an image appears online, supporting source, reuse and manipulation checks.

openness.note: The search tool is public, but it is a commercial reverse-image service rather than an open dataset or curriculum.

depth.note: Reverse image search is powerful for image provenance but narrower than full OSINT or media-verification training.

accessibility.note: Users can search by upload or image URL, making basic image checks approachable for nontechnical learners.

calm.note: The tool returns search results rather than attention-driven commentary.

economical.note: Basic reverse image search is available publicly, while TinEye also sells paid API and large-scale search services.

products.description: A reverse-image search tool for learning how to trace image reuse, older appearances and possible context collapse.

products.name: Hoaxy
products.brand: Indiana University Observatory on Social Media

educational.note: Hoaxy visualizes how claims and fact-checking spread online, making misinformation diffusion easier to study.

openness.note: Indiana University's Observatory on Social Media lists Hoaxy among its public tools and open-source resources.

depth.note: Hoaxy was built to study how misinformation and fact-checking spread and compete on social platforms.

accessibility.note: The visual interface helps explain spread patterns, but interpreting network graphs takes media-research context.

calm.note: The tool supports pattern analysis rather than dunking on individual posts.

economical.note: OSoMe's public tools are available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A misinformation-spread visualization resource for learning how claims, fact checks and sharing networks move online.

products.name: Botometer X
products.brand: Indiana University Observatory on Social Media

educational.note: Botometer X helps learners understand bot-likelihood scoring and why automated-account detection requires caution.

openness.note: OSoMe publishes Botometer X as part of its public social-media research toolset.

depth.note: A peer-reviewed tutorial frames Botometer as a public bot-detection tool while emphasizing model interpretation limits.

accessibility.note: Scores can be easy to overread, so the tool is best for learners who can treat outputs as probabilistic signals.

calm.note: The research framing encourages careful interpretation rather than labeling individual accounts with certainty.

economical.note: Botometer X is listed among OSoMe public tools without a listed user fee.

products.description: A social-bot research tool for learning why automated-account signals are useful, limited and easy to misuse.

products.name: Wayback Machine

educational.note: The Wayback Machine helps learners inspect past versions of web pages and preserve pages as trusted citations.

openness.note: The Internet Archive provides public search and Save Page Now access for web archives.

depth.note: Internet Archive help explains searching archived URLs by site name and date range, with limitations clearly noted.

accessibility.note: Save Page Now lets a user capture a page and receive a permanent URL for future reference.

calm.note: The archive supports evidence preservation and historical comparison rather than commentary.

economical.note: The Wayback Machine is publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A public web archive for learning how to compare changed pages, preserve sources and check historical context.

products.name: Perma.cc

educational.note: Perma.cc teaches link-rot literacy by letting people preserve cited web pages for future readers.

openness.note: Harvard Library describes Perma.cc as a preservation and citation tool supported by libraries and institutional partners.

depth.note: The tool focuses deeply on citation permanence rather than general web archiving or media verification.

accessibility.note: The public site supports sign-up and organization workflows, but durable institutional use often depends on library or court structures.

calm.note: The resource addresses source preservation with library infrastructure rather than urgency-driven content.

economical.note: Perma.cc has public sign-up, while institutional preservation workflows can depend on member organizations.

products.description: A link-preservation tool for learning why web citations rot and how to keep evidence available for later readers.

products.name: Hypothesis

educational.note: Hypothesis lets learners annotate, discuss and organize notes on web pages, PDFs and EPUBs.

openness.note: Hypothesis publishes its web-annotation software organization publicly on GitHub.

depth.note: The tool supports annotation, highlighting, tagging, group discussion and research organization rather than a full curriculum.

accessibility.note: A free personal account and browser extension let users start annotating web pages directly.

calm.note: Annotation supports slower reading and source engagement, though public annotations and classroom workflows can add social noise.

economical.note: Hypothesis says personal use and collaboration are free, with premium Education and Enterprise products separate.

products.description: A web-annotation tool for learning active reading, collaborative source discussion and research note-taking.

products.name: Zotero

educational.note: Zotero helps learners collect, organize, annotate, cite and share research sources.

openness.note: Zotero describes itself in support docs as a free, easy-to-use research-source tool and publishes public documentation.

depth.note: The quick-start documentation covers collecting items, organizing libraries, generating citations and sharing research.

accessibility.note: Zotero is available across major desktop and mobile platforms, with a quick bibliography option through ZoteroBib.

calm.note: The tool supports organized research workflows rather than attention-driven reading.

economical.note: Zotero is free to use, though optional storage or organizational needs can add costs.

products.description: A research-source manager for learning how to collect, organize, annotate and cite evidence cleanly.

products.name: ArchiveBox

educational.note: ArchiveBox teaches self-controlled web preservation by saving websites, bookmarks, media and research material into durable formats.

openness.note: The project describes ArchiveBox as open-source self-hosted web archiving.

depth.note: ArchiveBox can preserve HTML, PDF, PNG, TXT, JSON, WARC, MP4 and SQLite outputs.

accessibility.note: The tool is powerful but self-hosted and technical, with Docker and server setup as common paths.

calm.note: It supports deliberate evidence preservation and personal archives rather than platform feeds.

economical.note: The software is open source, though users need hosting, storage or infrastructure.

products.description: An open-source self-hosted archiving tool for learning how to preserve web evidence under your own control.

products.name: Webrecorder

educational.note: Webrecorder teaches high-fidelity web archiving for complex, interactive websites.

openness.note: Webrecorder says it provides open-source solutions and has developed open-source web-archiving tools for more than 10 years.

depth.note: Browsertrix supports dynamic websites, social media, crawl monitoring and signed outputs for chain of custody.

accessibility.note: The hosted platform lowers the barrier, but high-fidelity crawling remains a practitioner workflow.

calm.note: The toolset emphasizes preservation quality and replay rather than engagement metrics.

economical.note: Webrecorder offers open-source developer tools and a hosted Browsertrix platform with trial/commercial paths.

products.description: A high-fidelity web-archiving toolkit for learning how dynamic pages, social posts and interactive sites can be preserved.

products.name: Meta Ad Library

educational.note: Meta Ad Library helps learners inspect active ads and social, election or political ads that have run in the past.

openness.note: Meta describes the Ad Library as a comprehensive searchable database for ads transparency, but it remains a company-controlled dataset.

depth.note: The library and related tools expose ad records useful for learning about political and issue advertising patterns.

accessibility.note: The public search interface is approachable, though interpreting ad context and targeting remains difficult.

calm.note: The library is a record-search tool rather than a social feed, but it is still embedded in Meta's platform ecosystem.

economical.note: The public Ad Library search is available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A platform ad-search database for learning who is running ads on Meta services and how political or issue ads are disclosed.

products.name: Google Ads Transparency Center

educational.note: The center lets learners find active Google ads and extra transparency about election ads from around the world.

openness.note: Google publishes the center publicly, but the records are curated and controlled by the advertising platform.

depth.note: The tool includes advertiser search plus political advertising and paid YouTube product-placement transparency surfaces.

accessibility.note: The interface is public and searchable without requiring users to run their own data pipeline.

calm.note: The center presents ads as searchable records rather than feed content.

economical.note: The Ads Transparency Center is publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A searchable Google ads transparency surface for learning how advertisers, election ads and paid YouTube placements are disclosed.

products.name: TikTok Commercial Content Library

educational.note: The library helps learners inspect ads and other commercial content posted on TikTok.

openness.note: TikTok documents the library publicly, though its current support page limits included ads to EEA, Switzerland and UK contexts.

depth.note: TikTok's commercial content API includes ad data such as publication dates, impressions and selected targeting information for approved users.

accessibility.note: The public library is useful, but API access requires application and the available data is region-limited.

calm.note: The resource is a transparency library rather than the recommendation feed itself.

economical.note: TikTok documents the library and access process publicly without a listed user fee.

products.description: A platform transparency library for learning how TikTok exposes ads and commercial content, with important regional limits.

products.name: Snap Political Ads Library

educational.note: The library lets the public inspect political and advocacy advertising running on Snapchat.

openness.note: Snap provides public political and advocacy ad archives, but not a broad commercial ad database.

depth.note: The resource is useful for political-ad transparency, but narrower than full platform ad or targeting research access.

accessibility.note: Archive pages are public and organized by year, making basic inspection feasible.

calm.note: The library is a transparency record rather than a social feed.

economical.note: Snap's political ad archive is publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A narrower political-ad transparency library for learning how Snapchat discloses election and advocacy advertising.

products.name: Global Privacy Control

educational.note: GPC teaches browser-level privacy-rights signaling for do-not-sell-or-share and objection preferences.

openness.note: The W3C technical report documents the Global Privacy Control signal as a public specification.

depth.note: The FAQ explains how the signal can express legal privacy requests and where obligations may arise.

accessibility.note: GPC is available through several browsers, extensions and websites, reducing the burden of individual opt-out requests.

calm.note: The resource explains a persistent preference signal rather than encouraging repeated privacy-dashboard chasing.

economical.note: GPC information and the public specification are available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A privacy-rights signal resource for learning how browsers can communicate opt-out preferences automatically.

products.name: Privacy Badger

educational.note: Privacy Badger teaches tracker awareness by showing and blocking third-party tracking behavior in the browser.

openness.note: EFF describes Privacy Badger as its browser add-on and the Chrome listing identifies EFF as the maker.

depth.note: It focuses on invisible third-party tracking, not a complete privacy curriculum or full ad-blocking stack.

accessibility.note: EFF presents it as an install-and-forget add-on for common browsers.

calm.note: The tool reduces hidden tracking without requiring constant manual rule maintenance.

economical.note: Privacy Badger is publicly available as a browser extension without a listed user fee.

products.description: An EFF browser extension for learning how invisible third-party tracking works and how behavior-based blocking can reduce it.

products.name: No More Ransom

educational.note: No More Ransom teaches ransomware recovery basics and gives victims a place to look for decryptor tools.

openness.note: The project publicly describes its repository of keys and applications for decrypting files locked by ransomware.

depth.note: ECTEG describes the project as assisting recovery, raising public awareness and linking to national police agencies.

accessibility.note: The recovery flow is public and victim-oriented, though not every ransomware family has a decryptor.

calm.note: The site clearly notes that backups or security software are often necessary, avoiding false recovery guarantees.

economical.note: The project provides public guidance and decryptor lookup without a listed user fee.

products.description: A ransomware-response resource for learning what to do after an infection and when free decryptor tools may help.

products.name: StopRansomware.gov

educational.note: StopRansomware.gov is the U.S. government's official one-stop location for ransomware resources.

openness.note: CISA publishes the ransomware guide and resources publicly online.

depth.note: The #StopRansomware guide covers reducing ransomware likelihood and impact plus response checklist material.

accessibility.note: The resources are public and practical, but much of the guide is written for organizations rather than individuals.

calm.note: The guidance emphasizes preparation, mitigation and checklist-based response.

economical.note: StopRansomware.gov resources are publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A public ransomware preparation and response hub for learning prevention, checklist-based response and organizational recovery basics.

products.name: C2PA
products.brand: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity

educational.note: C2PA teaches content-provenance literacy through an open standard for origin and edit history of digital content.

openness.note: The coalition describes C2PA as an open technical standard for publishers, creators and consumers.

depth.note: The standard covers Content Credentials for establishing origin and edits of digital content.

accessibility.note: The concept is important for ordinary users, but the specification and ecosystem are technical.

calm.note: Content provenance gives users context about origin and editing rather than claiming to solve truth by itself.

economical.note: C2PA and Content Authenticity Initiative explainers are publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: An open content-provenance standard for learning how digital media can carry origin, edit-history and authenticity context.

products.name: TrueMedia.org

educational.note: TrueMedia helps learners understand deepfake and synthetic-media detection across images, videos and audio.

openness.note: The public site shares detection and policy insight goals, but the detection system is not an open public standard.

depth.note: TrueMedia says it analyzes system outputs, aggregate usage patterns and public feedback to inform deepfake and AI-fraud policy insight.

accessibility.note: The public-facing detector approach is easier for nontechnical users than forensic tooling, but detection outputs still need caution.

calm.note: The resource frames detection as one input into evidence and policy insight rather than a perfect truth machine.

economical.note: TrueMedia launched its detector as a free AI-enabled deepfake detection tool for newsrooms and public-interest use.

products.description: A synthetic-media detection resource for learning how deepfake checks can support, but not replace, careful verification.

products.name: National Digital Inclusion Alliance

educational.note: NDIA publishes definitions, resources and policy material that teach the language and practice of digital inclusion.

openness.note: The resource library is public and aimed at practitioners, advocates, academics, providers and policymakers.

depth.note: NDIA covers broadband affordability, digital skills, devices, digital navigators, policy and state digital inclusion work.

accessibility.note: The definitions and resource library are readable, though much of the material is practitioner-facing.

calm.note: NDIA frames digital equity through community programming and policy rather than consumer-tech hype.

economical.note: NDIA resources and definitions are publicly accessible online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A digital-equity resource hub for learning the terms, policy levers and community practices behind inclusive internet access.

products.name: Internet for All / Digital Equity Act Resources

educational.note: NTIA publishes technical-assistance resources for digital equity planning, coordination and implementation.

openness.note: BroadbandUSA resources and program pages are public government materials.

depth.note: The Digital Equity Act resource area covers planning guides, FAQs and local coordination resources.

accessibility.note: The materials are useful for communities and public agencies, but grant-program language can be dense.

calm.note: The guidance is programmatic and implementation-oriented rather than promotional.

economical.note: NTIA's technical-assistance resources are publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: Federal digital-equity planning resources for learning how communities structure access, adoption and skills programs.

products.name: Lifeline Support

educational.note: FCC and USAC pages teach who qualifies for Lifeline and how phone or internet discounts work.

openness.note: Lifeline program information is published publicly by the FCC and the USAC-run consumer site.

depth.note: USAC explains standard and Tribal benefit levels plus eligibility and application steps.

accessibility.note: The consumer site is organized around application and recertification steps.

calm.note: The guidance is benefits-oriented and procedural rather than advertising-driven.

economical.note: Lifeline provides up to a monthly service discount for eligible low-income subscribers, with enhanced Tribal benefits.

products.description: A federal phone and internet affordability resource for learning who can get connectivity discounts and how to apply.

products.name: FCC National Broadband Map

educational.note: The map teaches broadband-availability literacy by showing provider-reported internet services by location.

openness.note: The FCC publishes map, provider and coverage data publicly through Broadband Data Collection resources.

depth.note: The map includes fixed and mobile availability data and supports public challenges to improve accuracy.

accessibility.note: Address search and map views make local availability easier to inspect than raw broadband datasets.

calm.note: The map is a public data tool rather than a provider marketplace.

economical.note: The FCC National Broadband Map is publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A public broadband-availability map for learning how access data is reported, challenged and used in digital-equity planning.

products.name: ConnectHomeUSA

educational.note: ConnectHomeUSA explains digital inclusion for HUD-assisted housing residents and local implementation partners.

openness.note: HUD Exchange publishes program information and community resources publicly online.

depth.note: The program emphasizes connection at home for HUD-assisted housing residents and digital opportunity partnerships.

accessibility.note: The program page is oriented to communities and public housing authorities, so individual next steps depend on local participation.

calm.note: The resource frames connectivity as community infrastructure and resident support.

economical.note: HUD Exchange program information is publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A HUD digital-inclusion program resource for learning how housing communities connect residents to internet access and skills.

products.name: Human-I-T

educational.note: Human-I-T teaches digital-inclusion practice through services that combine devices, internet access, digital skills and tech support.

openness.note: The nonprofit publishes program and service information publicly, but it is a service provider rather than an open curriculum.

depth.note: Its organizational services cover low-cost devices, internet support and digital inclusion services for partner organizations.

accessibility.note: The model is practical for communities needing devices, internet and support, though availability depends on programs and eligibility.

calm.note: The resource frames access as social infrastructure and reuse rather than gadget marketing.

economical.note: Human-I-T offers low-cost devices, internet support and digital support rather than a purely free learning resource.

products.description: A digital-inclusion nonprofit for learning how device reuse, low-cost internet and support services work together.

products.name: PCs for People

educational.note: PCs for People shows how refurbished computers, low-cost internet and digital-skills support can close access gaps.

openness.note: The nonprofit publishes eligibility, device and internet-access information publicly.

depth.note: PCs for People covers affordable computers, internet solutions, digital skills training and technical support.

accessibility.note: Eligibility criteria and get-tech pages help low-income users understand whether they can use the service.

calm.note: The service pages are practical and eligibility-focused rather than device-marketing heavy.

economical.note: PCs for People provides refurbished computers at affordable prices and low-cost high-speed internet solutions for eligible customers.

products.description: A low-cost device and internet nonprofit that makes digital inclusion tangible through eligibility, refurbishing and support.

products.name: Digitunity

educational.note: Digitunity teaches device-access literacy by focusing on the systems that make computer ownership possible.

openness.note: Digitunity publishes resource-hub material on technology, research and digital-equity practice.

depth.note: Its Device Essentials for Digital Equity resource explains factors needed for successful device adoption and use.

accessibility.note: The materials are public and practical, though some are oriented to nonprofits and digital-equity practitioners.

calm.note: Digitunity frames device access as infrastructure and system design rather than consumer purchasing.

economical.note: Digitunity's resource pages are publicly accessible online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A device-equity resource for learning why computer ownership, support and reuse are central to digital inclusion.

products.name: PLA Digital Literacy Resources

educational.note: PLA compiles resources for libraries running hotspot lending, digital literacy training and public computer access programs.

openness.note: The Public Library Association publishes digital literacy resources and playbooks publicly.

depth.note: PLA resources include training ideas, library playbooks and DigitalLearn-aligned community instruction materials.

accessibility.note: The resources are built for public libraries that teach basic digital skills in community settings.

calm.note: The library framing emphasizes community support and practical skill-building.

economical.note: PLA digital literacy resource pages are publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: Public-library digital literacy resources for teaching basic skills, lending technology and supporting community access.

products.name: Library Freedom Project

educational.note: Library Freedom Project teaches privacy, intellectual freedom and critical technology through library-centered resources and trainings.

openness.note: Its free resources page publishes posters, bookmarks, presentations and teaching materials for privacy and information democracy.

depth.note: Library Freedom Institute covers privacy, intellectual freedom and critical technology for library workers over a multi-week program.

accessibility.note: Public resources and library-worker training help communities learn privacy through trusted local institutions.

calm.note: The project uses community education and library practice rather than panic-driven privacy advice.

economical.note: Library Freedom Project's free resource materials are publicly available online.

products.description: Library-centered privacy and critical-technology resources for learning how public institutions can teach safer digital life.

products.name: CPJ Digital Safety Kit

educational.note: CPJ's Digital Safety Kit is a starting point for journalists who want to improve digital safety.

openness.note: CPJ publishes the broader Safety Kit publicly with physical, digital and psychological safety resources.

depth.note: The kit covers risk assessment, device security, phishing, account protection and border-related precautions.

accessibility.note: The guidance is written for journalists and newsrooms and starts with practical risk-assessment advice.

calm.note: CPJ frames safety through preparation and threat modeling rather than fear.

economical.note: CPJ safety resources are publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A journalist-focused digital safety starter kit for learning risk assessment, account protection and safer reporting habits.

products.name: RSF Digital Security Guides

educational.note: RSF's digital security helpdesk explains encryption, journalist safety concepts and current tool recommendations.

openness.note: RSF publishes safety and digital-security resources for journalists publicly online.

depth.note: The RSF Safety Guide for Journalists is available in multiple languages and covers preparation before, during and after risky assignments.

accessibility.note: The helpdesk guide is useful for journalists, but it assumes some familiarity with security tools and reporting risks.

calm.note: The resource emphasizes practical concepts, tools and legal basics for journalists.

economical.note: RSF guides are publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: RSF safety resources for learning digital-security basics, assignment preparation and journalist risk reduction.

products.name: Coalition Against Online Violence

educational.note: The Online Violence Response Hub provides women journalists, newsrooms and allies step-by-step resources to combat online abuse.

openness.note: The hub and training resources are publicly accessible online.

depth.note: IWMF's newsroom guide details policies and best practices for protecting staff targeted with online violence.

accessibility.note: Self-paced training and step-by-step resources lower the barrier for newsrooms and individual journalists.

calm.note: The materials emphasize preparation, newsroom policy and support rather than leaving targets to react alone.

economical.note: The online violence hub and resource pages are publicly available without a listed user fee.

products.description: A journalist online-violence response hub for learning defensive planning, newsroom policy and digital-safety support.

products.name: Right To Be Resources

educational.note: Right To Be publishes resources and trainings on responding to harassment, including online harassment.

openness.note: The nonprofit provides free public resources and free training opportunities alongside private training offerings.

depth.note: Resource topics include online harassment, bystander intervention, resilience, workplace harassment and public harassment.

accessibility.note: Short guides and trainings make response strategies approachable for targets and bystanders.

calm.note: The resources emphasize concrete tools, support and intervention choices.

economical.note: Right To Be lists free resources and free training experiences publicly online.

products.description: Harassment-response resources for learning practical intervention, support and online-abuse response strategies.

products.name: Chayn Online Safety Resources

educational.note: Chayn publishes survivor-centered resources including DIY online safety and evidence collection guides.

openness.note: Chayn's resource page makes safety and abuse-response materials available publicly in many languages.

depth.note: Resource topics include online safety, evidence of abuse, domestic abuse case-building and technology-facilitated risks.

accessibility.note: Guides are written for survivors and are offered across multiple languages.

calm.note: The resources are survivor-centered and practical rather than blame-oriented.

economical.note: Chayn resources are publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: Survivor-centered online safety resources for learning how to reduce technology-facilitated abuse risks and document harm.

products.name: CyberPeace Builders

educational.note: CyberPeace Builders teaches nonprofit cybersecurity practice through volunteer missions such as assessments, awareness, scanning and incident response.

openness.note: Protect.ngo publicly explains the program model, matching platform and nonprofit support pathway.

depth.note: CISA lists Protect.ngo Foundation Cyber Builders as free cybersecurity assistance for under-resourced organizations.

accessibility.note: The program targets vetted nonprofits and depends on volunteer matching, so it is less self-serve than a course.

calm.note: The program emphasizes concrete missions, capacity-building and incident-response support.

economical.note: CISA describes the program as offering free cybersecurity assistance to under-resourced organizations.

products.description: A nonprofit cybersecurity support program for learning how civil-society organizations can get practical help with threats and response.

products.name: SAFETAG

educational.note: SAFETAG teaches security-audit practice for advocacy groups by adapting penetration testing and risk assessment to small nonprofits.

openness.note: The SAFETAG framework and method materials are published publicly online.

depth.note: Internews describes SAFETAG as a framework for organizational security audits and digital safety training for civil society.

products.description: A curated reading library for people connecting digital rights, climate justice and sustainable internet practice.

products.name: Sustainable Web Design

educational.note: Sustainable Web Design explains a people-and-planet approach to digital products, services and data.

openness.note: The site publicly explains the Sustainable Web Manifesto principles and links guideline material for web teams.

depth.note: The site introduces principles, guidelines and carbon ratings, but it is a practical framework rather than a full technical curriculum.

accessibility.note: The language is approachable for designers, developers and teams who need a starting framework for lower-impact digital services.

calm.note: The site is a focused reference and manifesto resource, not an engagement-driven learning product.

economical.note: The principles and carbon-rating explanations are public online without a listed reader fee.

products.description: A practical framework for understanding lower-impact web design through efficiency, openness, resilience and honesty.

products.name: Web Sustainability Guidelines

educational.note: W3C's Web Sustainability Guidelines explain how to design and implement digital products and services that put planet, people and prosperity first.

openness.note: The W3C report and quick reference are public, with feedback and development routed through open W3C/GitHub processes.

depth.note: The guidelines cover UX design, development, hosting, business strategy and measurable sustainability practices.

accessibility.note: The material is standards-style guidance and can be dense for nontechnical learners.

calm.note: The resource is standards guidance rather than a commercial or attention-driven learning platform.

economical.note: The W3C guideline text and quick reference are publicly accessible online.

products.description: The standards-track reference for teams learning how sustainability applies to web design, hosting and product practice.

products.name: Website Carbon Calculator

educational.note: Website Carbon Calculator estimates a page's carbon impact to raise awareness and inspire lower-impact web design.

openness.note: The calculator is free to use, but it is a Wholegrain Digital tool rather than a fully neutral open-data commons.

depth.note: The tool gives a simple carbon estimate and prompts action, but a single-page estimate is only a starting signal.

accessibility.note: The tool is simple for nontechnical users: enter a URL and receive a grade-style report.

calm.note: The calculator is task-focused, though it also sits inside a consultancy's broader sustainable web services ecosystem.

economical.note: Wholegrain describes the tool as free to use.

products.description: A simple public calculator for teaching that web pages have measurable energy and emissions consequences.

products.name: carbon.txt

educational.note: carbon.txt teaches a web-native approach for making organizational sustainability data discoverable and machine-readable.

openness.note: The carbon.txt ecosystem is described as open source and free to use and build on.

depth.note: Green Web Foundation developer docs explain the purpose and implementation model for carbon.txt.

accessibility.note: The idea is simple, but implementation is most useful to web teams, sustainability teams and data consumers.

calm.note: carbon.txt is a specification-style disclosure tool rather than a feed, course marketplace or brand campaign.

economical.note: The carbon.txt specification and related developer documentation are public online.

products.description: A technical disclosure pattern for learning how sustainability claims might become more discoverable and comparable on the web.

products.name: Ecograder

educational.note: Ecograder helps learners inspect website performance, sustainability and accessibility signals in one report.

openness.note: Ecograder is a public free tool, but it is operated by a commercial agency rather than a fully open public institution.

depth.note: Mightybytes says Ecograder uses metrics for performance, accessibility and environmental impact to suggest improvements.

accessibility.note: The tool gives a visible report from a URL, making digital sustainability easier to inspect without custom instrumentation.

calm.note: Ecograder is task-focused, though it also connects to Mightybytes' commercial services and expertise.

economical.note: Mightybytes describes Ecograder as a free web sustainability tool.

products.description: A free website audit tool that connects sustainability with performance, usability and accessibility signals.

products.name: Branch Magazine

educational.note: Branch is an online magazine about a sustainable and just internet, written by and for people working toward that goal.

openness.note: The magazine is publicly readable and funded/edited by Green Web Foundation for the volunteer-run Climate Action.tech community.

depth.note: Issues explore constraints, climate, infrastructure, design and justice through essays rather than short tips only.

accessibility.note: Branch is accessible as a public magazine, though essays can be more reflective and field-specific than beginner tutorials.

calm.note: The format is a magazine archive for slower reading, not a social platform or gamified learning app.

economical.note: Branch issues and articles are publicly available online without a listed reader fee.

products.description: A slower-reading magazine for understanding the politics, design and infrastructure of a just and sustainable internet.

products.name: web.dev Learn

educational.note: web.dev publishes courses and articles for building accessible, fast, secure, cross-browser websites.

openness.note: The learning material is publicly available, though it is maintained by Google/Chrome alongside external experts.

depth.note: web.dev includes dedicated learning paths for performance, accessibility and other web platform topics.

accessibility.note: The Learn Accessibility course is presented as an evergreen accessibility course and reference for web development.

calm.note: The site is a structured documentation and course hub, with vendor framing but little feed-style engagement.

economical.note: web.dev course and article content is publicly available online without a listed course fee.

products.description: A broad public web-development learning hub, strongest for performance, accessibility and modern web practice.

products.name: Can I use

educational.note: Can I use teaches browser support realities through up-to-date tables for HTML, CSS, APIs and modern web technologies.

openness.note: The site uses community-contributed support data and publishes browser support tables publicly.

depth.note: It gives detailed support tables and usage statistics, but is a reference database rather than a full course.

accessibility.note: The searchable table format lets learners and practitioners quickly inspect support for specific features.

calm.note: Can I use is a focused reference tool, not a feed, gamified app or ad-heavy learning platform.

economical.note: Browser support tables are publicly accessible online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A practical reference for learning that the web is not one browser, and that support data matters.

products.name: Internet.nl

educational.note: Internet.nl teaches modern internet standards by testing websites, email and connections for standards such as IPv6, DNSSEC, HTTPS, DMARC and RPKI.

openness.note: Internet.nl describes its code as available under an open-source license and its tests as based on open standards and public guidance.

depth.note: The report explanation documents the test norm and points to open standards, NCSC-NL advice and relevant IETF RFCs.

accessibility.note: The tool translates technical standards into website, email and connection tests, though some remediation details remain technical.

calm.note: Internet.nl is a public test-and-explain tool rather than a commercial marketing funnel.

economical.note: The tests and explanatory pages are publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A public standards-checking tool that makes internet reliability, security and email-authentication basics visible.

products.name: Let's Encrypt Documentation

educational.note: Let's Encrypt documentation explains free TLS certificates and practical steps for enabling HTTPS on websites.

openness.note: Let's Encrypt describes itself as a free, automated and open certificate authority run by nonprofit ISRG.

depth.note: The docs and FAQ cover certificate issuance, domain validation, renewal, rate limits, chain behavior and operational details.

accessibility.note: The material is public but most useful to people who administer domains or websites.

calm.note: The documentation is maintained by a nonprofit infrastructure project and is not an engagement-driven course platform.

economical.note: Let's Encrypt provides certificates and documentation without charging certificate fees.

products.description: Official docs for learning how HTTPS certificates work and why free automated TLS changed the web.

products.name: Web Almanac

educational.note: Web Almanac is HTTP Archive's annual state-of-the-web report, combining data trends and expert interpretation.

openness.note: The report is public and backed by HTTP Archive data and community expertise.

depth.note: The 2025 edition includes 16 chapters spanning page content, user experience, publishing and distribution.

accessibility.note: The report is readable online, though many chapters assume some familiarity with web performance or development concepts.

calm.note: The Web Almanac is an annual report archive, not a feed or product upsell.

economical.note: Web Almanac chapters are publicly available online without a listed reader fee.

products.description: An annual, data-backed report for understanding what the web is actually made of and how it changes.

products.name: HTTP Archive

educational.note: HTTP Archive teaches the shape of the web through public reports and detailed crawl data about real websites.

openness.note: HTTP Archive offers a public dataset through Google BigQuery and downloadable data for offline analysis.

depth.note: The archive includes request and response metadata, response bodies, execution traces and state-of-the-web reports.

accessibility.note: The dataset is powerful but technical, especially for learners new to BigQuery, HTTP or web performance metrics.

calm.note: HTTP Archive is a public research dataset and reporting project rather than a course marketplace or attention feed.

economical.note: The website reports and dataset access routes are public; BigQuery use may depend on a user's Google Cloud setup.

products.description: A public web-crawl dataset and report system for studying performance, security, page weight and web standards at scale.

products.name: Open Web Docs

educational.note: Open Web Docs supports web platform documentation for the benefit of web developers and designers worldwide.

openness.note: Open Web Docs is a public, donor-supported documentation project working on shared open web infrastructure.

depth.note: Its transparency reporting describes ongoing work to maintain and improve web platform documentation.

accessibility.note: Open Web Docs is more of an infrastructure steward than a step-by-step course, so learners mostly benefit through MDN and related docs.

calm.note: The project supports documentation infrastructure rather than pushing learners into a commercial or social platform.

economical.note: Its public reports, repositories and supported documentation work are accessible online without a listed reader fee.

products.description: A public-interest project behind better open web documentation, useful for understanding docs as digital infrastructure.

products.name: Common Crawl

educational.note: Common Crawl helps learners and researchers understand large-scale web data through a free public crawl archive.

openness.note: Common Crawl says it is a nonprofit that freely provides web crawl archives and datasets to the public.

depth.note: The archive includes WARC-format crawl data collected since 2008 and published in very large monthly crawls.

accessibility.note: Common Crawl is powerful but highly technical; beginners need comfort with WARC files, large datasets and analysis tooling.

calm.note: The project is a dataset and research infrastructure, not a polished course; use requires judgment about copyright, privacy and dataset limits.

economical.note: Common Crawl describes its archives as freely provided to the public.

products.description: A massive open web-crawl dataset for advanced learners studying search, AI, public web data and web-scale research tradeoffs.

products.name: Digital Beacon

educational.note: Digital Beacon lets users calculate a web page's environmental impact, inspect the breakdown and learn possible improvements.

openness.note: The tool is public, but it is a beta product by Aline rather than a standards body or open public dataset.

depth.note: Digital Beacon gives practical page-level impact reports, but its scope is narrower than full sustainability guidelines or infrastructure research.

accessibility.note: Users can submit a URL or use a bookmarklet to generate a report for the page they are visiting.

calm.note: The tool is a direct calculator with reports rather than a feed or course platform.

economical.note: The calculator is publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A lightweight page-level digital carbon calculator that makes the environmental cost of individual web pages concrete.

products.name: Cochrane Evidence Essentials

educational.note: Cochrane describes Evidence Essentials as an introduction to evidence-based medicine, clinical trials and Cochrane evidence for patients and the public.

openness.note: Cochrane lists Evidence Essentials as a free course and beginner's guide to health evidence.

depth.note: The course introduces evidence-based medicine, clinical trials, evidence synthesis and how to understand Cochrane reviews.

accessibility.note: The course is explicitly designed for patients, the public, policy makers and healthcare-team members rather than only researchers.

calm.note: The resource is a structured evidence-learning course rather than a feed, health-product funnel or symptom-search interface.

economical.note: Cochrane presents Evidence Essentials as a free course.

products.description: A public-friendly course for learning how health evidence, trials and reviews work before acting on health claims.

accessibility.note: The site is written for patients and consumers, with explanations of health topics and treatment tradeoffs.

calm.note: The site uses an independent public-health information model with no ads, influencer framing or product shopping path.

economical.note: IQWiG states that its health information for the public is free of charge.

products.description: An independent, ad-free health information source for comparing treatment benefits and harms in plain language.

products.name: Know the Science

educational.note: NCCIH says Know the Science helps people understand complex scientific topics related to health research and make informed health decisions.

depth.note: The initiative covers reading journal articles, supplement interactions, placebo effects, health news stories, risks and natural-product myths.

accessibility.note: NCCIH frames the materials as engaging and straightforward for consumers.

calm.note: The NIH source teaches how to judge evidence and health claims without selling products or prompting medical panic.

economical.note: The Know the Science materials are publicly available from NIH online.

products.description: NIH tools for judging health research, supplement claims, placebo effects and “natural” product marketing.

products.name: Ask for Evidence

educational.note: Ask for Evidence helps people ask what evidence lies behind health claims, news stories, ads and policies.

openness.note: Sense about Science publishes the tools and guides publicly as part of its public-interest evidence work.

depth.note: The resource explains types and quality of evidence, but it is a practical question-asking toolkit rather than a full research course.

accessibility.note: The campaign explicitly tells users they do not need to be experts to ask useful questions about evidence.

calm.note: The toolkit supports curiosity and specific questions rather than outrage or viral debunking.

economical.note: Ask for Evidence guides are publicly available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: A practical evidence-questioning toolkit for ads, policies, health claims and confident-sounding public statements.

products.name: Understanding Health Research

depth.note: The tool prompts users to consider funding, peer review, ethics, study quality and whether findings apply to their circumstances.

accessibility.note: The tool is designed to help non-specialists and patients make sense of published health research.

calm.note: It is a structured appraisal tool with reminders to speak to health professionals before applying findings personally.

economical.note: The health research appraisal tool is publicly available online without a listed fee.

products.name: Informed Health Choices

products.description: A claim-evaluation framework for deciding whether treatment and intervention claims are trustworthy.

openness.note: The site says the English original and translations are available for free download, with some audiobook versions.

depth.note: The book addresses treatment testing, research reliability and how patients and professionals can improve healthcare research.

calm.note: The resource teaches careful treatment evaluation rather than selling therapies or triggering symptom-search behavior.

products.name: CDC Health Literacy

products.description: A public-health literacy hub for people creating or judging understandable health communication.

products.name: NIH News in Health

educational.note: NIH News in Health is a monthly newsletter with practical health information based on NIH research findings.

openness.note: NIH says the material is not copyrighted and may be reprinted with acknowledgement.

accessibility.note: NIH frames the newsletter as practical consumer health news and information based on NIH research.

products.description: A plain-language NIH newsletter for learning practical health topics without commercial wellness marketing.

products.name: Understanding Science

depth.note: The climate hub links evidence, causes, effects, mitigation/adaptation and NASA climate-data context.

products.name: Security Education Companion

accessibility.note: The materials are written for new trainers who are not yet sure where to start.

products.name: Privacy Framework Learning Center

calm.note: NIST presents structured privacy-risk management guidance rather than urgent news or outrage-driven content.

products.name: Get Cyber Safe
