products.name: Harmony Square

educational.note: Harmony Square is an interactive game about online manipulation that highlights common tactics used to spread disinformation.

openness.note: The Harmony Square game is available to play online and is listed as a public information-literacy resource.

depth.note: The game is short and tactic-focused rather than a full media-literacy curriculum.

accessibility.note: InformationLiteracy.gov describes Harmony Square as an interactive game for players ages 15 and older.

calm.note: The game teaches manipulation tactics through role play; useful, but intentionally simulates divisive disinformation behavior.

economical.note: Harvard Misinformation Review describes Harmony Square as a short, free-to-play online game.

products.description: A short prebunking game that teaches political-disinformation tactics by letting players see how manipulation works from the inside.

products.name: Go Viral!

educational.note: WHO says Go Viral! helps users learn common ways false and misleading COVID-19 information is spread.

openness.note: The game is available online and was developed by Cambridge psychologists with DROG and the UK Cabinet Office.

depth.note: Go Viral! is a five-minute game focused on pandemic misinformation rather than a broad media-literacy program.

accessibility.note: WHO describes Go Viral! as a short game that improves users' ability to spot misinformation about COVID-19.

calm.note: The resource is brief and educational, but it focuses on pandemic misinformation and may feel dated or stressful for some users.

economical.note: WHO describes Go Viral! as an online game and does not list a player fee.

products.description: A short misinformation-inoculation game focused on pandemic falsehoods and the manipulation tactics behind them.

products.name: Cranky Uncle

educational.note: Cranky Uncle uses cartoons and critical thinking to help people recognize misinformation techniques.

openness.note: The game is available free on iPhone, Android and as a browser game.

depth.note: Cranky Uncle is supported by educator materials and explanations of the science behind the game.

accessibility.note: The game uses humor, cartoons and quizzes rather than a long text-heavy course.

calm.note: The resource teaches misinformation patterns through humor, though its examples often involve climate and science denial.

economical.note: Cranky Uncle says the game is available for free across mobile and browser platforms.

products.description: A humor-based game for learning the rhetorical tricks used in science denial and other misinformation.

products.name: Cyber Essentials Readiness Tool

educational.note: NCSC describes Cyber Essentials resources and a readiness tool that helps organizations implement the Cyber Essentials controls.

openness.note: Cyber Essentials guidance and the readiness tool are public resources, though certification itself is a formal paid scheme.

depth.note: IASME says the readiness tool walks through a questionnaire to gauge cyber security in relation to Cyber Essentials requirements.

accessibility.note: The tool turns organizational security controls into guided questions, but it is still aimed at small organizations rather than individuals.

calm.note: The resource supports steady readiness work rather than incident-driven cyber news.

economical.note: NCSC lists the readiness tool as a free resource even though Cyber Essentials certification has separate costs.

products.description: A guided readiness path for small organizations trying to understand basic cyber controls before formal certification.

products.name: Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 Small Business Quick-Start Guide

educational.note: NIST's small-business guide helps small and medium organizations kick-start cybersecurity risk management using CSF 2.0.

openness.note: NIST publishes CSF 2.0 quick-start guides and translations as public resources.

depth.note: The guide connects small organizations to CSF 2.0 cybersecurity outcomes and practical risk-management starting points.

accessibility.note: The guide is intended for organizations with modest or no cybersecurity plans, but it still uses framework language.

calm.note: The guide supports deliberate planning and prioritization rather than crisis-based security learning.

economical.note: The quick-start guide is publicly available from NIST without a listed fee.

products.description: A serious but useful bridge from personal cyber hygiene into small-organization security planning.

products.name: More Than a Password

educational.note: CISA explains that taking an extra step beyond a password can protect business, purchases, bank accounts and identity.

openness.note: CISA publishes public MFA guidance and Secure Our World materials online.

depth.note: The resource is a focused MFA explainer rather than a broad cybersecurity curriculum.

accessibility.note: CISA writes the MFA advice for ordinary account protection, with practical examples of where MFA helps.

calm.note: The page frames MFA as a simple protective step rather than a fear-driven security warning.

economical.note: CISA MFA guidance is publicly available online without a listed fee.

products.description: A simple public explainer for why MFA matters, useful as an entry point before choosing password managers or security keys.

products.name: Cyber Wardens
products.brand: Council of Small Business Organisations Australia

educational.note: Cyber Wardens offers a free online cyber-security course for small business owners and employees.

openness.note: The course is publicly advertised and free to enroll, though it is a branded program rather than open educational content.

depth.note: Cyber Wardens is framed as simplified cyber security for Australian small business rather than a technical deep-dive.

accessibility.note: The program emphasizes simple online learning for small business owners and employees.

calm.note: The training is organized as proactive small-business education rather than urgent incident response.

economical.note: Cyber Wardens describes the course as free and government-funded.

products.description: A practical small-business cyber-safety course, especially relevant for Australian organizations and nontechnical staff.

products.name: Exercise in a Box

educational.note: NCSC describes Exercise in a Box as a resource for testing and practising cyber-attack response.

openness.note: The overview says the tool is completely free and can be used by organizations in their own time.

depth.note: NCSC lists micro and tabletop exercises across topics such as ransomware, phishing, supply chain, risk management and passwords.

accessibility.note: The page says users do not have to be experts, though the material is aimed at organizations rather than solo learners.

calm.note: The exercises are designed for practice in a safe environment before a real incident.

economical.note: NCSC states the resource is completely free.

products.description: Free cyber-incident rehearsal exercises for small organizations that need to practise response before a crisis.

products.name: Awareness and Cyber Hygiene

educational.note: ENISA says its awareness work promotes good cybersecurity practices, behavioural change and everyday cyber hygiene.

openness.note: The hub publishes campaigns, events, publications and public cyber-hygiene material from the EU cybersecurity agency.

depth.note: ENISA connects awareness campaigns to regulatory developments, technical advances and everyday risk mitigation.

accessibility.note: The material serves citizens, private sector and authorities, but some pages assume EU policy context.

calm.note: The hub frames cybersecurity as habits and resilience rather than only incident alerts.

economical.note: ENISA publishes the awareness hub and related public materials online without a listed learner fee.

products.description: An EU public-resource hub for cyber-hygiene campaigns, citizen awareness and organizational security culture.

products.name: AR-in-a-Box

educational.note: ENISA describes AR-in-a-Box as a solution for designing and implementing cybersecurity awareness activities.

openness.note: The ENISA page presents AR-in-a-Box as a public resource for public bodies and private organizations.

depth.note: The resource is intended to provide both theoretical and practical knowledge for cybersecurity awareness programs.

accessibility.note: It is useful for program builders, but less direct for an individual looking for quick personal safety advice.

calm.note: The toolkit is designed for planned awareness work rather than emergency response.

economical.note: ENISA makes the AR-in-a-Box page publicly available without a listed fee.

products.description: A structured ENISA toolkit for people building cybersecurity awareness programs in organizations.

products.name: Public Awareness and Prevention Guides

educational.note: Europol says its crime-prevention guides contain information to help citizens protect themselves and their property.

openness.note: The guides are published by Europol as public awareness material.

depth.note: The material is prevention-oriented and broad, not a full technical cybersecurity curriculum.

accessibility.note: Europol frames the guides for citizens, making them useful for non-specialist safety learning.

calm.note: The guides emphasize prevention steps rather than sensational threat reporting.

economical.note: Europol publishes the awareness guide page online without a listed fee.

products.description: Citizen-facing crime and cybercrime prevention guidance from the EU law-enforcement agency.

products.name: Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr

educational.note: The official site says it assists victims, raises awareness of cyber risk and informs users about digital threats and protections.

openness.note: Cybermalveillance.gouv.fr publishes prevention and assistance material publicly as a French public-interest service.

depth.note: The service combines awareness, threat information and victim-assistance pathways rather than a formal academic course.

accessibility.note: The site serves individuals, businesses, associations, local authorities and administrations, though much content is France-specific.

calm.note: The resource gives structured prevention and victim-assistance paths instead of only threat-news updates.

economical.note: The public site is available online without a listed user fee.

products.description: French public cyber-safety and victim-assistance guidance, useful as a model for practical scam and incident response literacy.

products.name: Own Your Online
products.brand: New Zealand National Cyber Security Centre

educational.note: Own Your Online offers an online security assessment, exposure checks and practical security guidance.

openness.note: The NCSC says Own Your Online is part of government work to raise cyber-security awareness for New Zealanders and small businesses.

depth.note: The resource is practical personal and small-business cyber hygiene rather than deep technical training.

accessibility.note: The site gives customized action plans from a behavior-and-habits assessment.

calm.note: The assessment format turns online security into a step-by-step improvement plan.

economical.note: Own Your Online is a public government resource with no listed fee for the assessment or guidance.

products.description: A plain-language cyber-safety assessment and action-plan site from New Zealand's cyber agency.

products.name: Take Five to Stop Fraud

educational.note: Take Five provides advice to help people protect themselves from fraud through the Stop, Challenge, Protect habit.

openness.note: The campaign publishes public fraud-prevention advice, though it is led by UK Finance rather than a government agency.

depth.note: The campaign is a concise scam-awareness habit, not a broad financial-crime or cybersecurity curriculum.

accessibility.note: The core advice is intentionally simple and action-oriented for ordinary requests for money or information.

calm.note: Stop, Challenge, Protect is a measured pause-and-check routine for suspicious contact.

economical.note: Take Five publishes the consumer guidance online without a listed fee.

products.description: A memorable fraud-literacy campaign for slowing down suspicious requests for money or personal information.

products.name: Phishing Quiz

educational.note: The quiz asks whether users can spot phishing and gives practice identifying suspicious messages.

openness.note: The quiz is public, but it is a Google/Jigsaw-hosted branded tool rather than open curriculum.

depth.note: It is a short interactive quiz, useful for recognition practice but not comprehensive security training.

accessibility.note: The format is a simple public quiz designed around common phishing judgments.

calm.note: The tool teaches pattern recognition without relying on breaking-news threat alerts.

economical.note: The public quiz page is available without a listed fee.

products.description: A quick, interactive phishing-recognition exercise that is useful for beginners and workplace refreshers.

products.name: Digital Enquirer Kit

educational.note: Tactical Tech says the e-learning course teaches misinformation prevention, media literacy, verification and safer internet navigation.

openness.note: The project page says the course is available on the free atingi.org learning platform.

depth.note: The kit covers misinformation, verification and safer research habits for civil society and online information users.

accessibility.note: The course is designed as self-paced e-learning, though some topics are framed for civil-society and investigation contexts.

calm.note: The kit teaches deliberate verification practices rather than reactive outrage or viral-content tracking.

economical.note: Tactical Tech describes the course as available on a free platform.

products.description: A practical media-literacy and verification course for people who need to navigate misinformation and online research safely.

products.name: BEE SECURE

educational.note: The Better Internet for Kids profile describes BEE SECURE as Luxembourg's safer internet centre for awareness, counselling and reporting.

openness.note: The profile lists public awareness resources, a helpline and a stopline within the European safer-internet network.

depth.note: BEE SECURE is broad youth and family digital-safety support, not a deep technical course.

accessibility.note: The programme is designed for children, young people, parents, teachers and educators.

calm.note: The resource emphasizes positive digital culture and support rather than fear-based internet-safety messaging.

economical.note: The public safer-internet profile and resources are available online without a listed learner fee.

products.description: Luxembourg's safer-internet programme for youth, families and educators, with awareness and support pathways.

products.name: R for Data Science (2e)
products.brand: Hadley Wickham, Mine Cetinkaya-Rundel, Garrett Grolemund

educational.note: The online book teaches importing, tidying, transforming, visualizing and communicating data with R.

openness.note: The authors state the website is and will always be free, under a CC BY-NC-ND license.

depth.note: The table of contents covers data visualization, transformation, import, programming and communication workflows.

accessibility.note: The book is free online, but assumes willingness to learn R and data-science tooling.

calm.note: The book is a structured long-form text rather than an attention-driven course feed.

economical.note: The authors state the website is free, with a paid physical copy optional.

products.description: A free, rigorous, practice-oriented data-science book for learning R, visualization, data cleaning and reproducible analysis.

products.name: Python Data Science Handbook

educational.note: The site contains the full text and covers IPython, NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib and machine learning with scikit-learn.

openness.note: The site says the content is available as Jupyter notebooks, with text under CC BY-NC-ND and code under MIT.

depth.note: The table of contents covers core Python data libraries plus a machine-learning section.

accessibility.note: The book is free online, but it assumes some comfort with Python and notebooks.

calm.note: The resource is a static long-form reference rather than an ad-driven learning feed.

economical.note: The full text is published online, with buying the book suggested as optional support.

products.description: A free online handbook for Python data work, especially useful for moving from digital literacy into hands-on analysis.

products.name: DeepLearning.AI Short Courses

educational.note: DeepLearning.AI describes its course catalog as foundational specializations and skill-specific short courses taught by AI leaders.

openness.note: The catalog is public, but courses are platform-hosted and certificate or membership terms can vary by course.

depth.note: The catalog lists many practical AI topics, including prompt engineering, agents, RAG, LLMOps, evaluation and AI safety.

accessibility.note: The catalog includes beginner and intermediate courses, but many are oriented toward technical or workplace learners.

calm.note: The course catalog is practical but also closely tracks fast-moving AI tooling and vendor collaborations.

economical.note: DeepLearning.AI lists short courses and certificate programs in one catalog, so affordability depends on the selected course path.

products.description: A fast-moving AI course catalog with many practical short courses; useful, but more platform- and vendor-linked than open education.

products.name: OpenAI Academy

educational.note: OpenAI Academy offers AI Foundations for learning AI basics, large language models, ChatGPT, instructions, context and responsible use.

openness.note: OpenAI Help describes OpenAI Academy as a free, publicly accessible learning hub, though it is vendor-authored.

depth.note: The academy is strong for practical AI use but less neutral than independent AI-literacy curricula.

accessibility.note: The AI Foundations course is marked as suitable for people new to AI.

calm.note: The content teaches practical AI use, but it is also a product-adjacent learning hub for a fast-moving vendor ecosystem.

economical.note: OpenAI Help says the academy is free and publicly accessible.

products.description: A free OpenAI-authored AI basics hub; useful for practical ChatGPT literacy, but best paired with independent AI-ethics sources.

products.name: Anthropic Academy AI Fluency Courses

educational.note: Anthropic lists AI Fluency courses for foundations, educators, students, nonprofits and small businesses.

openness.note: The catalog is public, but it is hosted on Skilljar and is vendor-authored rather than open curriculum.

depth.note: The AI Fluency course descriptions emphasize effective, efficient, ethical and safe collaboration with AI systems.

accessibility.note: Anthropic says users do not need an Anthropic account to access the learning content, though a Skilljar account is required.

calm.note: The courses frame AI fluency as responsible collaboration, but are still connected to Anthropic's product ecosystem.

economical.note: The course page does not list a fee, but it does require Skilljar access and account terms.

products.description: Vendor-authored AI fluency courses that are practical for Claude users while requiring the usual caution around product-centered learning.

products.name: AI Skills Navigator

educational.note: Microsoft says AI Skills Navigator gives personalized recommendations for AI learning paths based on goals, skill level and learning style.

openness.note: Microsoft publishes the AI skills hub publicly, but many linked resources sit inside Microsoft, LinkedIn or partner ecosystems.

depth.note: The hub spans educator, nonprofit, public-sector, leader, responsible-AI and cybersecurity pathways.

accessibility.note: The navigator is explicitly designed to help learners choose a path from their goals and current skill level.

calm.note: The site is structured around skills pathways, but it is also tied to workforce-readiness and product ecosystems.

economical.note: Microsoft links a mix of public learning resources and partner pathways, so costs and account requirements can vary by path.

products.description: A Microsoft pathway-finder for AI learning; useful for workforce navigation, with vendor and partner lock-in caveats.

products.name: Mozilla AI Guide

educational.note: The guide teaches task selection, model evaluation, data provenance, bias checks and open-model workflows using summarization as a starting project.

openness.note: Mozilla explicitly frames the guide around avoiding dependence on closed-source or closed-data large language models when open options fit.

depth.note: The guide moves beyond prompting into dataset review, metrics, model choice and implementation.

accessibility.note: It is an approachable guide, but assumes comfort with technical AI evaluation and open-model workflows.

calm.note: Mozilla frames responsible AI as careful choices and evaluation rather than hype-driven adoption.

economical.note: The guide is publicly available online without a listed fee.

products.description: A Mozilla guide to using and evaluating open AI models responsibly, especially valuable as a counterweight to vendor-first AI literacy.

products.name: AI Blindspot
products.brand: MIT Media Lab / Berkman Klein Assembly

educational.note: AI Blindspot presents a discovery process for spotting unconscious biases and structural inequalities in AI systems.

openness.note: The site publishes cards and workshop material publicly online.

depth.note: The cards cover planning, building, deploying and monitoring concerns such as purpose, representative data, abusability and right to contest.

accessibility.note: The card format makes AI ethics concrete, though it is designed for teams or workshops more than solo beginners.

calm.note: The process encourages deliberate reflection on harms before and after deployment.

economical.note: The resource and downloadable cards are publicly available online without a listed fee.

products.description: A practical card-based process for teams learning to find bias, privacy and accountability risks in AI projects.

products.name: Build AI Knowledge and Literacy

educational.note: Google says the hub provides AI literacy resources and trainings for students, educators and families to use AI effectively, safely and responsibly.

openness.note: The hub is public, but it is Google-authored and includes product-specific paths for Gemini and Google tools.

depth.note: The hub spans teachers, higher education, high school students, families and youth internet safety.

accessibility.note: Google describes snackable educator sessions and separate pathways for families, students and teachers.

calm.note: The content is safety-framed but also product-forward around Google AI tools.

economical.note: Google says the AI Educator Series is available to educators free of charge, while some linked credentials or products can have separate terms.

products.description: A broad Google AI literacy hub for schools and families; useful for access, but explicitly product-adjacent.

products.name: Privacy Program

educational.note: Common Sense says the program evaluates privacy policies so parents and teachers can make smarter choices about learning tools.

openness.note: The site publishes privacy evaluations, ratings explanations, privacy questions and research publicly.

depth.note: The program includes privacy-policy evaluations, research reports and question sets for schools and districts.

accessibility.note: The program is useful for parents, teachers and administrators, though it is focused on child and student technology choices.

calm.note: The resource turns privacy decisions into evaluation questions and ratings rather than fear-based warnings.

economical.note: Common Sense says its privacy compliance software provides free privacy policy evaluations, while some related services may be separate.

products.description: A practical privacy-evaluation resource for parents, teachers and schools choosing education technology for children.

products.name: Online Privacy and Security

educational.note: The FTC hub teaches practical account, device, privacy and scam-protection basics for consumers.

openness.note: The advice is publicly available from a US consumer-protection agency without account signup.

depth.note: The hub links out to focused guides on passwords, phone security, malware, payment-app scams and personal information protection.

accessibility.note: FTC Consumer Advice is written for ordinary consumers and includes Spanish-language access on many pages.

calm.note: The material emphasizes concrete protective steps rather than panic or product promotion.

economical.note: The consumer guidance is free to read and use.

products.description: A plain-language public consumer hub for privacy, online security, device safety and scam avoidance.

products.name: Core Principles of Media Literacy Education

educational.note: NAMLE frames media literacy as inquiry, analysis, expression and civic participation across media forms.

openness.note: NAMLE publishes free media-literacy resources and identifies itself as a 501(c)(3) educational organization.

depth.note: The core principles connect media literacy to information, digital and social literacies rather than a single checklist.

accessibility.note: The principles are concise and public, though most useful for educators or curriculum designers.

calm.note: NAMLE emphasizes inquiry and mindful participation instead of fear-based media avoidance.

economical.note: The core-principles page and NAMLE resource hub are free to access.

products.description: A concise nonprofit framework for teaching media literacy as inquiry, creation and civic judgment.

products.name: OWASP Top 10

educational.note: OWASP describes the Top 10 as a standard awareness document for developers and web application security.

openness.note: OWASP publishes the project openly on the web through a nonprofit open-community security model.

depth.note: The current OWASP Top 10 release presents consensus risks and detailed application-security guidance.

accessibility.note: The resource is freely readable but assumes web-development or security vocabulary.

calm.note: OWASP frames security risk as structured awareness and remediation, though the material is dense and risk-focused.

economical.note: The Top 10 project is free to access.

products.description: The standard developer-facing awareness document for common web application security risks.

products.name: *Privacy Not Included

educational.note: Mozilla describes the guide as a way to make smarter choices and read expert privacy reviews of connected products.

openness.note: Mozilla publishes review pages and explains the warning-label approach and minimum security standards publicly.

depth.note: The guide evaluates product privacy and security against stated minimum standards and review criteria.

accessibility.note: The product-review format is consumer-friendly and organized by recognizable device and app categories.

calm.note: The warning-label style is useful but can feel more alarm-oriented than a neutral curriculum.

economical.note: The buyer's guide is free to read.

products.description: A consumer-facing privacy review guide for connected products, apps and AI-adjacent services.

products.name: Media Bias Chart

educational.note: Ad Fontes says it rates news sources for reliability and bias to help users understand the media landscape.

openness.note: Ad Fontes publishes methodology details, but its fuller data platform is a commercial product.

depth.note: The methodology page describes nonpartisan content analysis by trained analysts with reliability and bias dimensions.

accessibility.note: The chart is visually useful for quick comparison, though interpreting chart placement takes some context.

calm.note: A two-axis chart can invite comparison without outrage, but it can also over-compress contested editorial judgments.

economical.note: Ad Fontes offers public chart access while deeper tools and data services are commercial.

products.description: A recognizable news reliability and bias chart with a public methodology, best used as one signal rather than a final answer.

products.name: Media Bias Ratings

educational.note: AllSides uses media-bias ratings to present perspectives across the political spectrum and encourage broader news reading.

openness.note: AllSides publicly explains that it combines editorial reviews, blind bias surveys and other methods for ratings.

depth.note: The method is multi-input and useful for bias awareness, though it is not a full accuracy or source-quality curriculum.

accessibility.note: The ratings and balanced-news format are easy for non-specialists to understand.

calm.note: AllSides is designed around comparing perspectives, but political-bias labels can still trigger shortcut thinking.

economical.note: Many ratings and articles are public, while some products and memberships can be paid or limited.

products.description: A mainstream bias-awareness tool that helps users compare perspectives, with enough method disclosure to use cautiously.

products.name: NewsGuard Media Literacy

educational.note: NewsGuard offers media-literacy tools for students, libraries, educators and citizens evaluating online information.

openness.note: NewsGuard publishes rating criteria, but the ratings product itself is a commercial subscription service for many users.

depth.note: NewsGuard describes analyst-produced nutrition labels using specific criteria and publisher outreach before publishing ratings.

accessibility.note: The browser-extension format can be easy in classrooms and libraries, but access depends on subscriptions or institutional availability.

calm.note: Nutrition labels add context at the point of reading, though red/green trust signals can oversimplify contested judgments.

economical.note: NewsGuard advertises a free trial followed by a monthly subscription for direct consumer access.

products.description: A commercial but method-disclosing news-source context tool, useful in libraries and classrooms where access is available.

products.name: eSafety Commissioner

educational.note: eSafety provides online safety information, classroom resources and support pathways for children, parents and educators.

openness.note: The resource pages and classroom materials are publicly available from Australia's online-safety regulator.

depth.note: The classroom resource library covers privacy, device safety, cyberbullying, money online and getting help.

accessibility.note: eSafety serves students, parents, educators and people experiencing online abuse, with practical navigation by audience.

calm.note: The site pairs safety education with complaint and support pathways rather than only warning about harms.

economical.note: The public safety guidance and classroom resources are free to access.

products.description: A government online-safety hub with practical resources for families, educators and people dealing with online harm.

products.name: Top Tips for Staying Secure Online

educational.note: The NCSC collection teaches core public security habits such as separate email passwords, updates and two-step verification.

openness.note: The advice is publicly available from the UK's National Cyber Security Centre.

depth.note: The guidance is intentionally basic and actionable rather than a deep professional security curriculum.

accessibility.note: NCSC writes this collection for people and families rather than specialists.

calm.note: The page organizes security into a small number of doable habits.

economical.note: The public guidance is free to access.

products.description: A compact public-security guide for ordinary people who need a few high-impact habits, not a cybersecurity course.

products.name: Cyber Readiness Program

educational.note: CRI describes its program as helping small and medium businesses build practical cybersecurity habits.

openness.note: The program is available online and free, but it is a guided program rather than open educational source material.

depth.note: The program covers common small-business cyber vulnerabilities and organizational readiness basics.

accessibility.note: The self-paced format is aimed at small and medium-sized businesses rather than security professionals.

calm.note: CRI frames cyber risk as practical readiness and habit-building for businesses.

economical.note: CRI states that the online program is free.

products.description: A free small-business cybersecurity program focused on practical habits and organizational readiness.

products.name: Digital Skills and Jobs Platform

educational.note: The EU platform offers learning paths, training catalogues, resources and self-assessment tools for digital skills.

openness.note: The platform is a public EU hub, though individual linked trainings can have separate providers and terms.

depth.note: The platform aggregates learning resources, paths, self-assessments and policy/good-practice material.

accessibility.note: The hub is organized for European learners and workforce actors, but the catalogue breadth can be complex.

calm.note: The platform frames digital skills as structured learning and workforce development rather than fear-based urgency.

economical.note: The public platform is free to browse, while linked courses may vary by provider.

products.description: A public EU hub for digital skills, training paths, self-assessment and workforce learning resources.

products.name: Media and Information Literacy

educational.note: UNESCO's MIL program develops curricula, handbooks, MOOCs and digital-competency resources to empower citizens.

openness.note: UNESCO publishes media and information literacy resources and partner materials publicly.

depth.note: The resource collection includes curricula, publications, recommendations and frameworks for media and information literacy.

accessibility.note: The hub is global and public, though some materials are policy or educator oriented rather than quick consumer tips.

calm.note: UNESCO frames media literacy as citizen empowerment, trust and competencies rather than outrage or partisan sorting.

economical.note: UNESCO's media and information literacy pages and resource lists are free to access.

products.description: A high-level global media and information literacy hub with curricula, frameworks, publications and policy resources.

products.name: Spot the Troll

educational.note: The quiz teaches users to distinguish legitimate social accounts from troll accounts using real social-media content and feedback.

openness.note: The public quiz and resources are free on the web, though it is not presented as open-source curriculum.

depth.note: The quiz has eight profiles with explanatory tips, making it a focused practice tool rather than a full media-literacy course.

accessibility.note: A browser quiz with immediate answers is easier to use than a long course, though it depends on visual social-media examples.

calm.note: The resource frames deception as a learnable pattern and gives tips after each answer instead of relying only on fear.

economical.note: Spot the Troll is a free public quiz.

products.description: A compact Clemson quiz for practicing whether social-media profiles look authentic or deceptive, strongest as a quick inoculation exercise.

products.name: Which Face Is Real?

educational.note: The site asks users to identify real faces versus StyleGAN-generated faces as a practical lesson in synthetic media.

openness.note: The page explains its creators, project context, image sources and methods, but it is a public demo rather than an open curriculum package.

depth.note: The tool is narrow and visual, useful for awareness of AI-generated faces but not a complete deepfake-literacy curriculum.

accessibility.note: The interaction is simple and free, though it relies heavily on visual comparison.

calm.note: The University of Washington context frames the site as skill-building about synthetic faces rather than panic about all images.

economical.note: The public game is free to use on the web.

products.description: A simple synthetic-face practice game from the Calling Bullshit team, useful for seeing how plausible AI-generated faces can look.

products.name: Fakey

educational.note: Indiana University describes Fakey as a news-literacy game where players fact-check false information and avoid sharing junk content.

openness.note: Fakey is public on the web but is not presented as an open-source curriculum or lesson library.

depth.note: The game focuses on social-feed behavior, clickbait and false reports rather than broad news-literacy instruction.

accessibility.note: The live site is browser-based, though it depends on a JavaScript app and a social-feed game format.

calm.note: The learning frame is practice with responsible social-media consumption, though game scoring can make it feel less reflective than a guided lesson.

economical.note: Fakey is available as a free public web game.

products.description: A social-feed news-literacy game from Indiana University's Observatory on Social Media, useful for practicing when to share, like, or fact-check.

products.name: NOVA Cybersecurity Lab

educational.note: PBS LearningMedia describes the game as teaching digital safety, cyber scams, coding basics and defense against attacks.

openness.note: The learning resource is public through PBS LearningMedia, but not an open-source lab environment.

depth.note: The NOVA segment introduces core protection concepts but is not a deep professional cybersecurity course.

accessibility.note: PBS LearningMedia lists the lab for grades 6-8 and 9-12, making it classroom-friendly for middle and high school.

calm.note: The NOVA framing emphasizes practical protection steps and learning rather than selling security fear.

economical.note: The PBS LearningMedia resource is free to access.

products.description: A PBS/NOVA cyber-safety game for middle and high school learners, good for a light introduction to scams, coding and defense concepts.

products.name: CyberStart America

educational.note: Official program pages describe CyberStart America as a free cybersecurity training platform with interactive challenges for high school students.

openness.note: The program gives access to learning resources but is a sponsored platform rather than open educational content.

depth.note: Army JROTC describes 200+ interactive challenges across passwords, vulnerabilities, scripting, cryptography, Linux and forensics.

accessibility.note: The strongest access path is for eligible U.S. high school, JROTC and Civil Air Patrol students rather than all learners.

calm.note: Game missions and leaderboards can motivate learners, but competition and scholarship framing can be less calm than self-paced public lessons.

economical.note: Official sources describe CyberStart America as free for eligible high school participants.

products.description: A U.S. cybersecurity challenge and scholarship pathway for high school learners, with strong hands-on depth but narrower eligibility than public courses.

products.name: CYBER.ORG

educational.note: CYBER.ORG provides cybersecurity education resources, curriculum and training for K-12 schools.

openness.note: The site advertises free cyber lessons and courses, though the materials are platform curricula rather than fully open-source content.

depth.note: CYBER.ORG publishes K-12 cybersecurity learning standards and curricula across grade levels and subjects.

accessibility.note: The search interface spans K-12 grade levels and classroom activities, making it usable for teachers looking for age-appropriate lessons.

calm.note: The resource frames cybersecurity as education and workforce development rather than consumer fear.

economical.note: CYBER.ORG describes its classroom cyber lessons and courses as free.

products.description: A free K-12 cybersecurity curriculum hub with grade-band standards, lessons and educator resources.

products.name: Girls Who Code

educational.note: Girls Who Code offers free summer programs, clubs and learning pathways for girls and nonbinary students.

openness.note: The programs and club curriculum are free to participants, but the curriculum is a hosted program rather than an open-source course repository.

depth.note: The clubs curriculum covers topics including web development, cybersecurity, game design and AI.

accessibility.note: Girls Who Code offers free clubs and pathways, with explicit programming for teen girls and nonbinary students.

calm.note: The program emphasizes friendly coding environments, community and career exposure rather than adversarial competition.

economical.note: Girls Who Code presents its major student programs as free.

products.description: A major free pathway for girls and nonbinary students learning coding, cybersecurity, AI and web development through clubs and programs.

products.name: Code.org AI Curriculum

educational.note: Code.org's AI page includes curricula, lessons, videos and professional learning for teaching how AI works and affects society.

openness.note: Code.org describes free lessons, activities and resources, but the ecosystem is a hosted curriculum platform.

depth.note: The AI curriculum spans elementary through high school topics including AI foundations, computer vision, generative AI, ethics and machine learning.

accessibility.note: The resource page is organized by grade bands and teacher professional-learning modules, supporting classroom adoption.

calm.note: Code.org frames AI learning around fluency, ethical judgment and agency for students rather than AI panic.

economical.note: Code.org presents the AI lessons and teacher resources as free.

products.description: A broad free AI curriculum hub for K-12 classrooms, with grade-banded lessons on AI concepts, ethics, computer vision and generative AI.

products.name: AI Ethics Curriculum for Middle School

educational.note: The MIT curriculum teaches middle-school students AI ethics through activities, teacher guides, assessments and materials.

openness.note: The PDF states the materials are licensed CC-BY-NC for noncommercial remixing with attribution.

depth.note: The curriculum includes 97 pages of lesson activities, teacher guides, assessments and discussion material.

accessibility.note: The curriculum is designed for middle-school students and includes many unplugged activities, though teachers must work from a long PDF.

calm.note: The activities frame AI ethics as informed reasoning, bias, classifiers and responsibility rather than hype.

economical.note: The curriculum PDF is free to access online.

products.description: A free MIT middle-school AI ethics curriculum with teacher guides and activities, strong for careful classroom discussion rather than quick self-study.

products.name: AI4ALL Open Learning

educational.note: AI4ALL describes Open Learning as an online program for high school students building problem-solving, technical and AI-impact understanding.

openness.note: Open Learning is described as free and online, but it is a hosted program rather than a fully open curriculum repository.

depth.note: The program focuses on introductory AI concepts, projects and social-impact problem solving for high school learners.

accessibility.note: AI4ALL explicitly welcomes high school students from groups underrepresented in AI and positions the program as approachable.

calm.note: The program frames AI around solving problems learners care about and understanding impacts, not racing to adopt tools.

economical.note: AI4ALL describes Open Learning as a free online program.

products.description: A free AI learning pathway designed especially for high school students from underrepresented groups, with a social-impact framing.

products.name: Break the Fake

educational.note: MediaSmarts' Break the Fake teaches four practical steps for checking whether online information is true.

openness.note: The public campaign pages and quizzes are freely accessible, though the materials are branded MediaSmarts resources.

depth.note: The resource is strongest as a practical misinformation-checking starter and quick quiz set rather than a full curriculum.

accessibility.note: MediaSmarts provides quick public quizzes and workshop-style resources for beginning fact-checking practice.

calm.note: The approach is a short checklist for checking source, fact-checkers, context and other coverage rather than panic scanning.

economical.note: The Break the Fake pages and quizzes are free public resources.

products.description: A practical MediaSmarts misinformation-checking campaign with quick quizzes and a simple verification routine for beginners.

products.name: News Literacy Project Quizzes

educational.note: NLP publishes short quizzes on journalism standards, pink slime sites, misinformation tactics, fact-checking red flags and AI.

openness.note: The quiz collection is publicly browsable, while the broader Checkology classroom platform uses registration.

depth.note: The quizzes are short practice checks, best paired with Checkology lessons or classroom discussion for depth.

accessibility.note: Short quiz formats lower the barrier for classroom warmups, family discussion or quick self-checks.

calm.note: NLP describes its work as helping students evaluate what they see, read and hear with care and curiosity.

economical.note: NLP says Checkology includes hundreds of free resources, including quizzes and downloadable lessons.

products.description: A set of short news-literacy quizzes for practicing misinformation, AI, fact-checking and local-news credibility skills.

products.name: MDN Web Accessibility

educational.note: MDN's accessibility hub teaches web accessibility concepts, assistive technologies, semantic structure, ARIA and inclusive web-development practice.

openness.note: MDN publishes the accessibility reference publicly and Mozilla's MDN content is developed as open web documentation.

depth.note: The accessibility area links into topic pages for HTML, CSS, JavaScript, ARIA, multimedia, testing and assistive technology.

accessibility.note: The material is explicitly framed around enabling people with limited abilities to use websites and web apps.

calm.note: MDN uses reference-style documentation and curriculum pages rather than engagement loops or gamified streak mechanics.

economical.note: The accessibility documentation is freely readable without course fees.

products.description: Mozilla's focused accessibility reference and curriculum for learning semantic HTML, ARIA, assistive technology and accessible web practice.

products.name: W3C Alt Decision Tree

educational.note: The WAI decision tree teaches how to decide whether an image needs alt text and what kind of alternative should be used.

openness.note: W3C publishes the decision tree as a public WAI tutorial resource.

depth.note: The resource is intentionally narrow and tactical, focused on image alternatives rather than a full accessibility course.

accessibility.note: Correct alternatives for images are a core accessibility practice for screen-reader users and other non-visual contexts.

calm.note: The page is a compact decision aid with no social feed or attention mechanics.

economical.note: The decision tree is freely available online.

products.description: A compact W3C decision aid for choosing useful alt text, empty alt text or other alternatives for images.

products.name: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide

educational.note: The APG explains how to apply accessibility semantics to common web design patterns and widgets.

openness.note: W3C publishes the guide publicly as part of WAI's ARIA resources.

depth.note: The guide includes patterns, keyboard interaction models, design examples and guidance for complex application widgets.

accessibility.note: The material is highly relevant to accessible custom interfaces, but it is technical and best suited to developers and designers with web basics.

calm.note: The guide is reference documentation with examples, not a gamified learning platform.

economical.note: The guide is freely available online.

products.description: The W3C reference guide for accessible custom widgets, keyboard behavior and ARIA patterns.

products.name: Making Audio and Video Media Accessible

educational.note: WAI's media guide teaches how to plan captions, transcripts, audio description and other accessibility requirements for audio and video.

openness.note: The guide is publicly published by W3C WAI.

depth.note: The guide covers planning, content, descriptions, captions, transcripts, media players and WCAG connections.

accessibility.note: The resource directly addresses accessibility for people who cannot hear audio, see video or use standard media controls.

calm.note: The resource is a structured reference and project-planning guide rather than a feed or course marketplace.

economical.note: The guide is freely readable online.

products.description: A W3C guide to captions, transcripts, audio description and planning accessible audio/video projects.

products.name: How People with Disabilities Use the Web

educational.note: The WAI resource introduces how disabled people use the web and why inaccessible digital products create barriers.

openness.note: W3C publishes the resource publicly as a WAI learning document.

depth.note: The resource includes stories, tools, techniques, abilities, barriers and examples, though it is introductory rather than a full technical curriculum.

accessibility.note: It centers diverse abilities, assistive technologies and real barriers experienced by disabled people online.

calm.note: The material is plain-language educational documentation with no social or addictive product mechanics.

economical.note: The WAI resource is freely available online.

products.description: A people-centered W3C explainer on disability, assistive technology and the barriers inaccessible digital products create.

products.name: DCMP Captioning Key

educational.note: DCMP's Captioning Key provides guidelines, examples and resources for captioning educational media.

openness.note: The Captioning Key pages are publicly browsable, while other DCMP services may require membership eligibility.

depth.note: The guide includes captioning philosophy, text, sound effects, synchronization, placement and quality criteria.

accessibility.note: DCMP says its captioning and description guidelines are developed for educational media accessibility.

calm.note: The resource is a reference guide for production practice, with no engagement feed.

economical.note: The Captioning Key guidance is freely readable online.

products.description: A practical captioning-standard resource for educational video, covering accuracy, synchronization, placement and readability.

products.name: Accessibility Insights

educational.note: Accessibility Insights teaches practical accessibility testing through guided checks for web pages, web apps and Windows apps.

openness.note: Microsoft says Accessibility Insights tools are open source and the project links to its GitHub repositories.

depth.note: The tool and docs support fast automated checks plus deeper assessment flows, but they do not replace a full accessibility curriculum.

accessibility.note: The web extension is designed to help developers find and fix accessibility issues in web apps against WCAG coverage.

calm.note: It is a task-oriented testing utility rather than a feed, marketplace or attention platform.

economical.note: Microsoft describes Accessibility Insights as free tools for finding and fixing common accessibility issues.

products.description: Free, open-source accessibility testing tools and docs that help developers learn by checking real web and Windows interfaces.

products.name: W3C Evaluation Tools List

educational.note: WAI's tools list explains that evaluation tools can help determine whether web content meets accessibility guidelines and links to tool-selection guidance.

openness.note: The list is publicly available and W3C notes that listed information is submitted by providers and others.

depth.note: The list is broad and filterable, but quality varies because W3C does not endorse listed tools.

accessibility.note: The resource is specifically about tools that check web accessibility guideline conformance.

calm.note: It is a searchable directory and reference page, not a gamified platform.

economical.note: The W3C list is free to browse and includes many free or trial tools, though individual tool pricing varies.

products.description: A public W3C directory for learning what accessibility evaluation tools exist and how to choose among them.

products.name: WebAIM Alternative Text

educational.note: WebAIM's alt text guide explains what alternative text is, why it matters and how to handle common image situations.

openness.note: The guide is publicly available as part of WebAIM's free resource library.

depth.note: The article covers core cases and examples for alternative text, but it remains a focused guide rather than a broad curriculum.

accessibility.note: Alternative text is presented as a textual substitute for non-text content, especially important to screen-reader access.

calm.note: The page is a plain instructional article with examples and no attention-driven mechanics.

economical.note: The WebAIM article is free to read online.

products.description: A practical WebAIM guide for writing useful alternative text for images and other non-text content.

products.name: WebAIM Screen Reader User Survey

educational.note: WebAIM's survey results help designers, developers and educators understand screen-reader-user preferences and reported barriers.

openness.note: The survey results are published publicly online.

depth.note: Survey 10 reports 1,539 valid responses across topics such as screen readers, browsers, landmarks, headings and problematic items.

accessibility.note: The dataset centers people who use screen readers and provides evidence for accessibility decisions beyond abstract assumptions.

calm.note: The report is a static research page rather than an engagement platform.

economical.note: The survey report is freely readable online.

products.description: WebAIM's public survey results on screen-reader usage, preferences and common accessibility barriers.

products.name: How to Meet WCAG Quick Reference

educational.note: The WAI Quick Reference gives a customizable view of WCAG 2 requirements, success criteria, techniques and understanding resources.

openness.note: W3C publishes the Quick Reference publicly as part of WAI's WCAG resources.

depth.note: The tool supports filtering WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 success criteria, techniques and supporting information.

accessibility.note: WCAG documents explain how to make web content more accessible for people with disabilities.

calm.note: It is a standards reference tool and filterable checklist rather than a course platform with retention mechanics.

economical.note: The Quick Reference is freely available online.

products.description: The W3C filterable reference for translating WCAG success criteria into practical techniques and checks.

products.name: USWDS Accessibility Guidance

educational.note: USWDS teaches accessibility principles, component guidance and inclusive federal web practice for product teams.

openness.note: The U.S. Web Design System publishes its accessibility guidance and component documentation publicly.

depth.note: USWDS combines accessibility principles with component-level UX, code and implementation guidance.

accessibility.note: USWDS says it follows the four accessibility principles of perceivable, operable, understandable and robust.

calm.note: The site is professional documentation for government service teams, not a social or gamified learning product.

economical.note: USWDS guidance is free to read and its toolkit is public.

products.description: Public U.S. government design-system guidance for building accessible, mobile-friendly services and components.

products.name: Data & Society

educational.note: Data & Society studies the social implications of data, automation and AI, producing research for informed public debate.

openness.note: The institute publishes a public library and states that site contents are Creative Commons licensed unless otherwise noted.

depth.note: Its work covers machine learning, AI systems, algorithmic impact, online infrastructure and technology governance.

accessibility.note: The material is rich and public-interest oriented, but many reports assume comfort with policy and social-science research.

calm.note: Data & Society is a research library and events publisher, not a feed-optimized course marketplace.

economical.note: Its public research library is freely accessible online.

products.description: A public-interest research institute for learning how data, automation and AI reshape work, institutions, power and public policy.

products.name: AlgorithmWatch

educational.note: AlgorithmWatch publishes investigations, reports and explainers on automated decision-making, AI and algorithmic accountability.

openness.note: AlgorithmWatch states that site content is CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise noted.

depth.note: The site includes journalistic stories, projects, positions and comprehensive publications on algorithmic decision-making impacts.

accessibility.note: The work is public and practical, but many investigations and EU policy analyses are dense for beginners.

calm.note: AlgorithmWatch is a nonprofit research and journalism site; it does not use course-streak or social-feed mechanics.

economical.note: Its stories, reports and publications are publicly readable without a paywall.

products.description: A nonprofit watchdog for learning how algorithmic decision systems affect rights, democracy, labor, sustainability and daily life.

products.name: Tech Policy Press

educational.note: Tech Policy Press publishes news, opinion and analysis at the intersection of technology, democracy and policy.

openness.note: Articles and podcasts are publicly browsable, with support requested through donations rather than a hard paywall.

depth.note: Its stated focus areas include platform power, technology and the economy, ethics, geopolitics, oppression and election integrity.

accessibility.note: The writing is more current-affairs and policy-analysis oriented than beginner curriculum, so it is best after basic digital-literacy grounding.

calm.note: The site is a news and analysis publication, so it is timely but naturally less calm than static reference resources.

economical.note: The publication's content is available to read online for free.

products.description: A nonprofit tech-policy publication for following platform power, AI governance, tech regulation, elections and democracy.

products.name: Deceptive Patterns

educational.note: The site teaches how deceptive patterns in apps, websites and AI systems steer people into actions they did not mean to take.

openness.note: The pattern taxonomy, examples, laws, enforcement actions and reading list are publicly browsable.

depth.note: The resource catalogs types such as hidden costs, hard-to-cancel flows, fake urgency, forced action and disguised ads.

accessibility.note: Short pattern definitions make the resource useful for consumers, educators and designers without needing formal UX training.

calm.note: It is a reference catalogue rather than a feed, game or engagement platform.

economical.note: The pattern library is free to browse online.

products.description: A practical pattern library for recognizing manipulative interface design, dark patterns and related enforcement examples.

products.name: The Glass Room

educational.note: Tactical Tech describes The Glass Room as an interactive exhibition that helps people understand how technologies and data change their lives.

openness.note: The project includes free virtual experiences plus assets such as interactive posters, animations, educational apps and exhibition materials.

depth.note: The Glass Room is more experiential than academic, but it links privacy, data, misinformation, AI and platform impacts through multiple formats.

accessibility.note: The project is designed for educators, schools, librarians, museums, community spaces and media-literacy promoters.

calm.note: Its self-learning exhibition format encourages reflection and discussion rather than quick-hit feeds.

economical.note: The virtual experience and many project materials are freely accessible online.

products.description: A public digital-literacy exhibition and virtual experience about privacy, misinformation, AI, data and everyday technology impacts.

products.name: Privacy International

educational.note: Privacy International publishes news, guides, campaigns and learning material on privacy, surveillance, profiling and digital rights.

openness.note: Its guides, learn section and campaign pages are publicly available.

depth.note: The site covers modern technologies and rights across topics such as surveillance, profiling, anonymity, data exploitation and state power.

accessibility.note: Privacy International mixes practical explainers with advocacy and long reads, so beginners may need to choose guides before reports.

calm.note: The resource is advocacy-forward but organized around reports and guides rather than attention mechanics.

economical.note: Public guides and learning pages are free to access online.

products.description: A digital-rights and privacy resource for learning how surveillance, profiling and data exploitation affect real freedoms.

products.name: Berkman Klein Center

educational.note: BKC publishes research and projects on internet governance, AI ethics, media, democracy, public discourse, privacy and technology law.

openness.note: Its publications, projects, topics and events are publicly listed online.

depth.note: Featured topics include ethics and governance of AI, media and democracy, technology law, and governance of technology and the internet.

accessibility.note: BKC is excellent for serious learners, but much of the material is university research rather than step-by-step beginner curriculum.

calm.note: The center publishes research, tools, events and topic pages without feed-optimized learning mechanics.

economical.note: Publications and topic pages are free to browse online.

products.description: A university internet-and-society research hub for deeper learning about AI governance, platform power, law and public discourse.

products.name: Tow Center for Digital Journalism

educational.note: Tow Center studies digital journalism, platforms and publishers, and provides journalists with skills and knowledge for digital journalism.

openness.note: The center publishes research, events and project pages publicly through Columbia Journalism School.

depth.note: Tow funds and publishes research into the intersection of newsrooms, emerging technologies and technology companies.

accessibility.note: Its strongest material is aimed at journalists and researchers, so consumer learners may need orientation from general news-literacy resources first.

calm.note: Tow is a research center with publications and free panels, not a social feed or course marketplace.

economical.note: The center's research pages and findings are publicly accessible online.

products.description: A digital-journalism research center for understanding how platforms, technology companies and newsroom economics shape information quality.

products.name: All Tech Is Human

educational.note: All Tech Is Human publishes responsible-tech and public-interest-technology resources, including reports, guides, reading lists and career pathways.

openness.note: Many reports, guides and resource lists are public, though parts of the community run through Slack and applications.

depth.note: The public-interest technology page links to guides, roles, competencies, outside resources and ecosystem organizations.

accessibility.note: It gives practical entry points for people seeking public-interest technology careers, organizations, books and community pathways.

calm.note: The resource is community-oriented and event-driven, but its guides and reports are browsable at a human pace.

economical.note: Public guides, reading lists and resource pages are free to access.

products.description: A responsible-tech ecosystem hub for learning public-interest technology pathways, organizations, reports, guides and ways to get involved.

products.name: Global Network Initiative

educational.note: GNI provides frameworks, learning resources and policy materials on freedom of expression and privacy in the technology sector.

openness.note: The site publicly hosts principles, resources, policy material, blog posts and legal-framework tools.

depth.note: GNI works across responsible decision-making, best practices, policy, accountability and member commitments for tech and telecom companies.

accessibility.note: The resource is useful for governance and policy learning, but its frameworks are less beginner-friendly than consumer guides.

calm.note: GNI is an institutional resource hub rather than a feed-optimized media platform.

economical.note: Principles and public resources are freely accessible online.

products.description: A multi-stakeholder digital-rights resource for learning how tech companies address privacy, expression and government demands.

products.name: Internet Safety Labs

educational.note: Internet Safety Labs publishes empirical research and safety labels that make invisible privacy and app-safety risks easier to understand.

openness.note: ISL publishes public reports, references, specifications and an App Microscope label resource.

depth.note: Its reports cover data brokers, identity resolution, edtech safety, app safety, policy positions and privacy research agreements.

accessibility.note: Safety labels and public reports translate technical app behavior into consumer- and policymaker-facing risks.

calm.note: The work is presented as reports and safety labels, not as an engagement feed.

economical.note: Reports and the public safety-label resources are free to access online.

products.description: A nonprofit testing lab and report library for learning about app privacy, data brokers, edtech safety and connected-product risks.

products.name: Integrity Institute

educational.note: Integrity Institute transforms platform trust-and-safety expertise into original research, best practices and policy guidance.

openness.note: The public research page includes reports, policy responses, articles and podcasts, while the expert community itself is member-based.

depth.note: Its research draws on hundreds of trust-and-safety professionals across many tech companies and countries.

accessibility.note: The content is strong for platform-governance learners, but often assumes policy, safety or platform operations context.

calm.note: The site organizes research and policy outputs as a library, not as a social media feed.

economical.note: Public research and articles are free to read online.

products.description: A trust-and-safety research resource for learning how platforms assess transparency, child safety, elections, ranking and online harms.
